comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: AMERICAS Mont Belvieu propane market values declined by a nickel over the second half of April, and by nearly a dime since the front of April.  Prices now are marked in the mid 70cpg range, but still a solid 39% of WTI (basis today’s $79.36/bbl value).  Most of the market seem to agree that the weight of the (sometimes slowly) growing inventory levels will push prices down over the summer, but it appears now that a legitimate trend is developing.  With regards the inventories, the EIA yesterday recorded what is perceived as a disappointing 200,000bbl build in overall stock levels (as of 26 Apr), where the market was anticipating something over/under 2mmbbls.  Higher export volumes combined with (still) strong production levels are the culprits.  With limited spot availability known to exist in June, the spot terminal fee market remains buoyant, with the last known deal done at just under 9cpg, but offers now seen at double-digits.  Buy-side interest exists in the upper single digits.  NWE  Northwest Europe, now in decline and off the double digits, was unexempt from the crude-driven sell off of global LPG prices.  Compounding the region’s downward pressure was the nearly 600,000 tons of LPG imported during April, and the return to service of Karstoe and Mongstad refineries in the North Sea.  That said, with US propane under the most pressure at present, the LST/NWE arbitrage is open again, which will no doubt attract more US East coast FOB volumes to already well supplied Western European terminals.

EAST Some Australia cargos and a WAF tender early in the week have helped shorten the Middle East Gulf position list and freight have come up slightly. Many of the remaining available ships are expected to seek employment in the West but there’s still a decent amount of vessels that are likely to remain in the East. Last decade May fixing in AG is well underway with 3 spot deals done already and we expect freight to be relatively stable to slightly positive for this period.  WEST So far this week we have only seen a couple deals done in the West and now we count 6 spot fixtures for June out of the USG/USEC. While one vessel still remains available for mid-May dates, some have already begun fixing for the second decade of June. The position list looking balanced to tight with five to six open vessels left 1-10 June while 10-15 June showing six open positions. Last done at mid/low 130s H/C.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG Saudi Aramco cut May CP to $580 for C3 and $585 for C4, down by $35 each. The price is in line with expectation, but the announcement time is earlier than what most expected. As of the drops in flat price and attractive discounts on FOBs, we are seeing buying demand from Indian major recent. HPCL tendered to buy two evenly split cargos for 2h May and Jun liftings ex AG and was reported to award on CFR basis to a producer trading arm, with netback at CP minus mid high teens reportedly. At the time of writing, Jun CP was traded at $545 and C3/C4 turned into positive at $5. Jun/Jul CP was traded at $7 backwardation.   FAR EAST Active bids for 23kt C3 parcel, especially for 2h Jun delivery into FAR EAST. On Thur, such parcel for 1h Jun delivery was bid at June FEI plus $7 and similar parcel for 2h delivery bid at plus $6, whereas few offers seen. 11/11 or 0/23 for 2h Jun delivery (including Us origins ) were offered at Jun FEI plus $5.5. Off window discussions slow down as of the ongoing labor day holiday.   However before the holiday, a handful of 46kt C3 were already placed into China at Jun FEI plus low teens basis Ningbo, and a 23kt C3 parcel also traded via tender at similar price. With the new PDH expansion and the marginal but positive profits we expect more feedstock inquiries after the holiday for 2h Jun arrival onwards. The China latest PDH run rates have improved close to  70%, with some units returned from maintenance and new startups.   Apart from PDHs, cracking demand continued its strength, we’ve seen FEI/MOPJ spread in minus 90s and 80s for May and June respectively. One Korean importer issued term tenders to secure 23kt butane for monthly delivery from Aug 2024 to Jan 2025 (6 lots) or to Jul 2025 (12 lots), and 23/23 or 23kt butane for Feb 2025 to Jan 2026 delivery.

Last week, there were smoke signals emanating from the USG  Aframax market, suggesting growing support for the wider Suezmax Atlantic market, but ultimately, availability of afra tonnage has thus far quashed this momentum and capped Suezmax (for now).    In West Africa, we should be about to close the books on the second decade, save for the odd straggler cargo but it's the third decade that could throw up a little volatility. Reports on the trading side suggests that end month Wafr stems are not the easiest to sell, which could make it a healthy Suezmax decade. When you also factor in the limited availability of Vlcc tonnage in the Atlantic for those dates, there is room for optimism,  In the East, whilst the list is fairly tight,  there has been a lack of surface-fixtures which will maintain a flat feeling in the region for the balance of the week. MEG/East trades WS 110 and BOT/UKCM WS60-62.5 via Cape.

This week began at a slower pace compared to the previous week, as many regions around the world observed holidays. Consequently, the LNG shipping market saw limited spot fixtures concluded.  Vessel availability remains slightly longer than the spot requirements seen this week and while spot charter rates have remained unchanged across all basins, there has been an increase in enquires and a slight upward trend in rates for multi-month and short-term charters. There are also some signs of the arbitrage opening again and although trading margins would be limited, the market is braced for some longer voyages. Thus, there are positive sentiments for spot and multi-month charters as both charterers and owners work towards bridging those gaps to align on period and rates.   Aside from the open arbitrage, the broader LNG product market remains stable, with supply more than able to meet current demand. Inventory levels in Japan and Korea are at comfortable levels, while European storage levels experienced a slight increase. There has been some suggestion of floating cargoes into July or August, given the anticipated slight weakness in June pricing, and this has the potential to improve shipping utilisation in the near term. With a well-supplied availability list, any rate rises would be modest.  In the LNG newbuilding segment, Qatar Energy has reportedly expanded its orders for 18 LNG Carriers of 271,000m3 with Chinese shipbuilder Hudong Zhonghua, at an estimated price of approximately US$310 million per vessel. Eight of these newbuilds are slated for delivery within 2028 and 2029, while the remaining ten vessels are scheduled for delivery between 2030 and 2031.

The situation across the tanker second hand market has remained largely the same over the past months, despite the usual volatility in the charter space. The climb in asset values show no sign of respite with very strong level of buying enquiry for modern eco tonnage being met by an ever-thinning list of available candidates. Newbuildings become therefore the avenue of choice where despite the continuous headlines of placed orders, the relative percentage of fleet renewal is still historically low. A flurry of 2009 blt Aframax tanker sales this week, showing the high demand from the Far East for ships of this type and vintage. GSTAAD GRACE II/AFRAGOLD 115K DWT New Times 2009, sold for USD 42M and 41M respectively with the formed freshly surveys passed, this will help price other units in the market.  Despite a fall in earnings on Capes this week, it seems buyers are not being discouraged by the resilient price targets from owners, with the overall vessel supply story trumping doubts of the longevity of this run. This is shown in scrubber fitted FRONTIER UNITY 181K DWT Koyo Dockyard 2012, selling to Greek buyers at USD 35M . A particularly busy week on the Supramax front, where Navios sold two Tess 58s NAVIOS CELESTIAL/CHRISTINE B 58K DWT Tsuneishi Zhoushan 2009 for USD 30M en bloc.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: AMERICAS The EIA reported a +1.00mmbbl build in overall US propane inventory levels, which is about half of what most in the industry had anticipated and which left total stocks at 56.70mmbbls as of 19 April.  This is roughly 97% of last year and 145% of two years ago.  Even so, many continue to predict that by the first week of October propane stocks will have reached the mid/upper 90mmbbl range, with some predictions reaching up to (and in some cases beyond) 100mmbbls as of that timeframe.  Meanwhile, MB propane prices closed up slightly yesterday, likely because US crude inventory draws of 6.3mmbbls gave cause for a bit of a runup in WTI values, though news of large-scale Russian crude production and export volumes tampered sentiments.  The terminal fee market on the Gulf Coast, however, remains robust.  A ~10cpg May deal was believed to have been fixed and as news that the terminals are expected to be tight in June made the rounds, asking levels for June moved upwards to nothing less than double-digits.  This is partially due to the fact that the shipping sector is well-balanced for the moment and therefore unable to grab a share of the slowly rising US/Far East arb.  NWE As of mid week, CIF ARA propane values are hanging around $505 /metric ton, with the large-cargo propane market  assessed at -$7/mt to May quotes, The propane/naphtha spread however, is assessed at -182pmt and continues to attract significant quantities of us LPG (an expected 520,000 tons for April) - well above the Q1 average of 430,000 tons, which has more than made up for reduced imports from the North Sea and Ust Luga, which remain hampered by maintenance and the enduring Russia and Ukrainian conflict, respectively.

EAST A freight tender in the Middle East managed to break the 60’s yesterday and another deal was done at very low 60’s. At the same time we’re seeing a more optimistic freight environment in the West which makes some people wonder if market has come off a bit too much in the region. Now most Owners are aiming to hold for 60’s and above. But we can’t ignore the fact that there’s still a decent length in the East and with Panama getting more congested, the long way back to the West via Cape makes earnings there less attractive than it looks at first sight.  WEST In the Western market we have seen a handful of spot fixtures out of the US Gulf so far this week, and we now count 31 deals in total for May dates – the year-to-date average is at 30 spot fixtures. There are still 3-4 open vessels (1 relet) left in May and with the currently slim FOB availability that month we could expect some waiting time for the ships still available. June fixing is already underway and we find last done fixture concluded in the high 120s H/C.

It has been a busy week in LNG shipping, with a handful of spot requirements, term requirements and cargo tenders being worked in the last few days. Spot rates have taken a slight dip in the Atlantic basin, due to some competitive sublet tonnage being offered at lower levels than a week ago, but in the Pacific, it has been a different story with charterers facing firmer rate levels especially for 2H May / 1H June cargoes. There are no drastic changes on the overall sentiment however, and we believe the spot market will remain rather stable for the weeks to come. There is some good news in Freeport ramping up production again, which could lead to some of the prompt tonnage disappearing in the US Gulf, although set against this is the news that Hammerfest has had another outage which may free up a few prompt vessels in Europe. The term market, or more specifically the 1-year TC market, has definitely been the focus for many this week and rates seem to be firming, as more charterers are looking to strengthen their portfolio over the winter, especially with modern 2-stroke tonnage. In the newbuilding market, although no new orders this week, yards are keeping busy with their existing building schedules.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG Qatar Petroluem awarded their sale tender for an end May lifting evenly split cargo at May Cp minus 30s. One trader is also offering similar cargo at fixed price of $555 in window on Thurs. 1st round Cp recommendation heard at $580-590s for C3 and C4 at $5 higher.   At the time of writing, May Cp was assessed at $590 and May/Jun Cp at $25 backwardation.   FAR EAST 23/0 parcels for 1h Jun delivery was bid at Jun FEI plus $7.5 while similar parcel for 2h Jun was bid at plus $6 vs offer at $18.  Several 46/0 parcels have been traded into China via tenders, with price at the range of Jun FEI plus high single to low teens level, depending on different locations. Before upcoming Labour Day holiday week in China, we expect some more buy tenders for Jun delivery, especially from some petchem players operating or supplying more than one unit.   Apart from Propane, Pertamina was reported to award two 22/22 for mid Jun arrival at Jun Cp plus 30s. IOC was also said to award May FOB AG 2/2 cargo at Cp minus 30s and Jun at minus 20s.

Healthy activity levels across the basin for geared sizes.  Commodity prices slowly getting back to normal. Markets continued to push in line with our expectations, albeit a bit stronger than seasonality suggests. See signs of market flattening and expect a sideways trend more in line with average seasonality for the remainder of the month and following month. After days of lackluster activity, we are finally seeing more cargo volumes ex ECSA. Given the improvement in commodity prices, there will be more cargoes coming in the market in the coming weeks. Period market remains strong with all major operators scouting the market for long period tonnage.

A couple of market quotes first thing this morning will breathe a bit of life into what has been a quiet MEG VLCC market. However, given the lack of other activity in the area, there remains a likely continued short-term softening ahead on a MEG/China run as charterers will try to push lower in to the WS 50’s. TD3 now WS 58 to test. However, as is increasingly the case, our market is often driven by other sizes - notably Aframaxes in the USG. These a fair bit busier overnight, 80 x WS 172.5 paid which is up 10 points and a number of cargoes still outstanding, so further upward pressure. Therefore, we are expecting a kick up on VLs here, certainly after 10 odd VLCCs reported ex Americas yesterday alone (and these are the ones we know of). USG/China now paying USD 8.6m and a healthy demurrage of USD 75k will give owners heart. West steady, busy and upside ahead.

The interconnected nature of the Atlantic market continues to maintain relatively tight trough/peak spreads when compared to pre-Ukraine war. The West African Suezmax market saw a Dalia/Sarroch cargo trade WS 90, which probably freights a TD20 run at WS 95 today and with USG/transatlantic Aframax's creeping up to 70kt x WS 172.5 overnight there is an expectation that the handbrake will immanently be applied to further falls.  In the East, MEG/India cargoes have dominated the week interspersed with the occasional fuel oil stem. We are freighting MEG/USG USD 5-5.1m whilst MEG/East probably has a floor at WS 105-110 basis NHC. The lure of the Atlantic market might drag BOT/UKCM down to mid/high WS 50's via Cape.

On the C5 front, we see a reasonably healthy level of enquiries from miners, operators, and tenders primarily for first half of May dates. Some operators were seen coming out for second half May and forward June dates as well. East Australia coal and volumes on other Pacific businesses have picked up with most having early to mid-May dates. Volumes out of South Africa remain relatively flat. On C3 ex Brazil to China and West Africa, volume of enquiries has continued to hold up from last week with a majority for June dates and some for late May dates. Far East tonnage is moderately abundant. Ballasting tonnage weighs on second half of May with some vessels still able to make first half of May dates. On C5, we see a downward trend thus far this week with fixtures concluding at mid USD 10 pmt levels by mid-week. On C3, fixtures concluded at mid USD 26 pmt levels for mid to late May dates.

NORTH SEA  Activity has been covering the last of the April/very early May stems with rates moving sideways.  First 5 days in May are not overly populated with stems, so with some tonnage coming back into the window we could see some downward pressure on the rates.  US Markets look to have bottomed and an increase in activity has seen rates bounce back a touch with a firmer sentiment, so ballasting out of North Sea still remains a very viable option for tonnage.   MEDITERRANEAN Mediterranean Aframaxes have seen consistent activity for the week with both replacement deals and cargoes working, but the market has held in a steady trend with sufficient tonnage there to fix. North Africa stems have pushed in to May mid first decade dates and onwards with activity expected to remain fruitful. Worth noting CPC blend is due some maintenance and forecasting a decrease in volume there although that might have an effect Suezmaxes more so.

This week in the Panamax market reflects a generally stable yet subdued tone with several regional nuances. The market closely mirrors typical seasonal patterns, anticipating a downturn in the coming month. In the Atlantic, activity has decreased, with most recent cargoes already covered, indicating potential rate adjustments downward, particularly as the North Atlantic stabilizes without significant momentum. Conversely, the ECSA remains relatively steady with decent demand projected from mid-May. The Pacific market show signs of weakening, especially from Indonesia due to a seasonal dip in coal demand, despite a stable tonnage count. Overall market sentiment is mixed, with some regions showing firmness in rates and cargo volume, but a clear lack of bids casts uncertainty on the true market value.

The tanker story remains unchanged from recent trends, with relatively modern (younger than 15 yo) sales candidates hard to come by, resulting in low liquidity. Money continues to flood the newbuilding yards giving an idea of the future make up of the global fleet, where we are seeing advancements in designs and fuelling, this week seen in the first ammonia dual-fuel aframax tankers being ordered by MISC (through shipping arm AET). In the second-hand market, Tsakos sold IZUMO PRINCESS (105K DWT SUMITOMO 2007) for USD 37.1M.   The bulk market continues to see fairly strong liquidity despite prices making many buyers in the market feel uneasy, even with the general positive market sentiment. Modern tonnage is still very popular with YMK QUARTET (82K DWT Jiangsu Yangzi-Mitsui 2021) being sold at USD 35M to Greek buyers. FEDERAL ISLAND (63K DWT TADOTSU SHIPYARD 2017) was sold for USD 32M, a firming against the last done 2017 blt unit SANTA JOHANNA (61K DWT SHIN KURUSHIMA 2017) at USD 30.5M back in February.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG Fob discounts for May liftings further deepened as of ample supply amid limited demand, especially evenly split cargos. KPC was reported to sell their mid May lifting heavy propane cargo at May Cp minus mid high 30s. Saudi Aramco released their May lifting acceptance and its trading company is fixing vessels for early May loadings.  May C3 Cp was traded at $584 and C4 at $588, May/Jun Cp was traded at $20 backwardation.  FAR EAST  Unlike the Fobs, premium on 23kt propane parcel for 2h May delivery was bid up to May FEI plus high single digit. And similar parcel for 1H June was bid at Jun FEI plus $7, while May/Jun FEI traded at $6.  A handful of tenders were floating again this week. One NChina PDH user awarded their buy tender for 46/0 2h May delivery at May FEI plus low teens reportedly. One SChina PDH also secured similar parcel at the mixture of FEI and Cp plus teens level. There are another two tenders ongoing for propane delivered into Hainan and Tianjin in 2H May to 1H Jun periods. One SChina cracker also issued two tenders for April and May LPG at flexible ratio but were reported canceled, perhaps ended up taking in special origin cargos, which was reported done at May Cp minus level for prompt delivery and mid high single level for May delivery.  Pertamina tendered to buy evenly split cargo for 8-12 Jun delivery. IOC issued mini term tender to secure similar ratio cargo for May to Jul delivery. HTC also called term tender to procure 23kt propane from Jul 2024 to Jun 2025 delivery.

Following the relatively quiet spell last week, there has been a significant upturn in spot chartering enquiries issued across both basins for May and June cargoes. Spot rates are experiencing a slight increase in the Atlantic but remain unchanged in the East. While there is an abundance of vessels in the available tonnage list, finding the perfect match for specific requirements can pose a challenge, particularly with some of the older vessels warming up. Interest in multi-month charters is also picking up and with periods through the upcoming winter, there is increasing visibility on market sentiment for the traditionally stronger months of the year. All of these market developments are happening under the shadow of more geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East, and although this unlikely to have a direct impact on the LNG shipping market (since the Suez Canal is already a no-go area) the wider impact on energy markets remains a risk. This week saw no newbuilding orders, with prices holding steady.

EAST Saudi Aramco released their acceptances for next month on Tuesday and as a result we saw a few more first half May cargoes hit the Middle East market. First decade spot count in May now stands at seven which makes it look like we soon will shift focus into the second decade of the month. Although we could see a couple of more cargos within the first 10 days of May – the vessel count in the same period surely puts a lid on any potential upside.  WEST A recent uptick in activity have resulted in a slight increase in western freight rates and almost all the positions left in 1H May USG are now programmed. With latest sub fixtures we currently count 24 spot fixtures for May USG/USEC. The vessel supply looks balanced in the second half of May, with the last deals concluded around the mid 120s H/C.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: AMERICAS Where inventory data expectations ranged widely from a build of around one million barrels to a high of as much as three million barrels, most of the market was clustered around the 2mmbbl build range.  The EIA yesterday, however, posted a build of 4mmbbls – well above most (if not all) expectations.    The initial shock soon gave way, however, to the generally accepted view that the large build likely included corrective data from weeks past, versus the idea that there might be a correction in the coming weeks.  In any case, stocks as of 13 April 2024 stand at 55.7mmbbls, which is almost exactly 100% of last year’s level – but still 150% of two years ago.    The MB pricing structure reacted immediately and sharply increased the rate of decline for non-TET propane values.  Currently MB c3 is pegged at the mid 78cpg range with the expectation that further price erosion is likely on the horizon.  In looking towards the end of the build season – typically the first week of Oct – most calculations put stock levels at around the 95mmbbl range, which is based on robust production levels, generally capped export volumes, flat(ish) chem consumption, warmer weather and (therefore) limited summertime res/com demand.  NWE At present,  Europe is projected to conclude  april having imported just shy of 500kt-  half of which  will discharge at Terneuzen. The regions resilient  demand comes on the back propane's  utilization versus  naphtha  at Europeans petrochemical plants- The East /west spread continues to widen, and econs are becoming less advantageous- but for now, cargoes especially from Marcus Hook, continue to sail toward NWE.

Positive sentiment across the Supramax sector with firmer numbers on the spot trading and period. South Atlantic and USG pushing indexes in green territories, bringing both TA and FH trips to better levels. The 10TC average closed today at USD 14,702.   Ultramax MV Al Wathba (63,555 dwt, built 2019) opened Veracruz on 24 April and heard about subs for USG/Japan with wood pellets at USD 26,000 pd. ECSA fixing healthy levels MV Valiant Sapphire (63,646 dwt, built 2023) fixed for TCT via Brazil at USD 17,775 + USD 775,000 GBB for Asia discharge. Transatlantic is now trading at around USD 15,000 pd.  Pacific market looks healthy with lots of fresh inequity appearing on the spot – prompt dates. Pacific China round trips fixing sub USD 15,000 pd.

The Panamax market is showing signs of a rebound, driven by an increase in ECSA grain shipments and a relative rise in the Panamax 82 index compared to the Supramax 63 index. Market sentiment remains positive despite mixed views and varying activities in different regions. In Asia, the market continues its upward trajectory with strong rates, while in the Atlantic, tonnage and cargo volumes are balanced, keeping rates stable. The ECSA market displays a dual pricing structure with spot tonnage at a discount versus premium May liftings. Overall, the Panamax market outlook is optimistic, with expectations of further rate improvements.

This week we have seen activity covering a lot of the 3rd decade dates which pushed rates up to WS 150 levels. Firmer market due to vessels continuing to leave the area and a lack of natural North Sea tonnage able to give options charterers require. With that being said, this morning a fixture was reported well-below last done levels which will affect sentiment somewhat. Tonnage list is still tight-ish but with dates moving forward and more vessels coming back in position a test might be needed for the first decade of May. The USG and Mediterranean markets look a little softer but still attractive to ballast from North Sea giving higher returns.  Activity in the Mediterranean has been more measured this week with some initial slower inquiry and then some action, as the final North Africa opportunities worked toward a close. April stems ex CPC and Ceyhan are complete and with early May dates now on the cards, forward tonnage looks able to deal with what’s to come in the short term and competition should keep downward pressure on rates for the time being. Sentiment suggests any movement should be gradual with owner’s resistant to allowing a significant softening of rates.

On the C5 front, we see enquires from miners, operators, and some tenders for late April to early May dates. Volumes out of East Australia and other Pacific businesses have seen improvement from the previous week with most enquiries ranging from early to mid-May dates. Volumes out of South Africa are a tick high but remain flat overall. On C3 ex Brazil to China and West Africa, volume of enquiries maintained from last week with majority for second half of May dates with some forward buying for June. Far East tonnage is moderately abundant. Ballasting tonnage weighs heavily on May with several drifters able to make late April dates. On C5, we see an upward trend through the week with fixtures concluding at mid USD 11 pmt levels by mid-week. On C3, we see the same trend with fixtures concluding at high USD 26 pmt levels onwards for mid-May dates. One known fixture of a 179k dwt, 2013-built, non-scrubbered for 16 to 18 months at USD 27,000 levels per day.

After last week’s spike in the Atlantic, enquiry, rates have cooled off with rates likely to be tested down. In West Africa, there were circa 21mb penciled in to lift for the first decade of May, of which we believe 16mb has gone on VLCCs and 2mb further cargoes have been lifted on Suezmax, leaving max' 3 stems to lift in that window. The USG appears a little more insulated against drastic softening for prompt laycans, but as May dates come into view, the list won't become as troublesome for charterers.   The East has been in slow mode for over a month now and despite the list not being the longest (comparatively speaking) there is a softer feel as we hit midweek.

A lackluster week in the MEG, as the week straddled the April and May cargo dates. As we awaited stem confirmations, the market has remained in the low WS 60’s. Present levels seem to be a happy medium. However, at the time of writing, charterers active/live in the market are moving slowly, countering up the WS 50’s in an effort to drag rates down. A brave game, certainly if there is any early May rush to come.  As for the Atlantic, we see very few Eastern ballasters at present, and the list can be described as ‘a little tight’. USG/East activity picked up approx USD 250k over the week but has since quietened. USG/Ningbo rates at the USD 8.65m level, done a couple of times, with a few cargoes still working/reported. Shell has been active from Brazil, reportedly taking 4 ships for first half May, but being “old news” not having an effect. It is likely busier than it seems on the surface, with 4-5 ships rptd on subs, no details.   Lethargic, but not without hope.

A jolt of life in the tanker second hand market this week with a handful of transactions to report amongst the smaller sizes, otherwise, a fairly subdued week as Ramadan came to an end. In the standout transaction, D’Amico bought AMFITRION (50K DWT SAMSUNG HI NINGBO 2017) for USD 43.5M, compare that to the last sale of a similar Chinese MR SUNNY APATITE (50K DWT GSI 2016) at USD 34M, one can see just how much the market has shifted in the last two quarters. In the high value and tight STST market where levels continue to rise, Delos Shipping bought CHEM BULLDOG (21K DWT ASAKAWA 2010) at USD 23M.  We are entering a critical period in this most recent dry market rally. Levels and buying interest have been ever increasing over the last quarter, however, as a consequence some buyers are now being priced out and others are perhaps pulling back to observe whether prices will remain high, or will correct in the short term. Scrubber fitted Kamsarmax SAMMY (82K DWT Tsuneishi 2012) sold at USD 24.6M, surprisingly softer than the initial market rumours pricing the deal closer to USD 26M. Capes continue to be in demand with the sale of scrubber fitted HL HARMONY (179K DWT DALIAN 2015) to Hong Kong based buyers at USD 43M.

text: MEG Low buying sentiment for May with a handful of evenly split cargos offered in the market, from both importers and traders resale availabilities. Offers for May loaders reported asked at May CP minus teens while few bids heard. May CP was traded at $590 for C3 and C4/C3 at $5. May/Jun CP was traded at $15 backwardation.   FAR EAST CFR east discussion level also softened this week compared to last week, seeing bids for 23/0 parcels for 2h May delivery at May FEI plus $2 only and offers assessed at plus high single digit. Outside window a couple of 46kt propane for 1h May delivery into North and East China are concluded at May FEI plus mid-teens level.   Several buy tenders into China ongoing this week. FIC tendered to buy 46/0 for late May delivery des Ningbo at May FEI plus high single, which is the 2nd purchase for their PDH on May delivery. Another Echina cracker also issued buy tender for 23/0 or 46/0 des Ningbo during mid May, whose last tender only awarded 23/0 for earlier May delivery. However, due to scheduled maintenance (which resulted in general run rate lower than 60%)  and unstable trial run on new PDHs we are expecting limited buying interests on May. Apart from C3, One Schina importer awarded their buy tender for 11/11 2h May to early Jun delivery at May FEI and Jun CP related price reportedly.

EAST Adnoc dates were published yesterday, and prior to this, we already registered a couple of May fixtures in the Middle East Gulf. With vessel availability remaining long, freight has so far failed to move much upwards despite a widening gap between theoretical East and West earnings – but last done is now slightly above yesterday’s Baltic.   WEST We have seen a few spot fixtures in the West this week and we now count about 10 deals for May dates out of the US. The current position list indicates a balanced to tight market, with around 5-6 vessels remaining available for the first decade of May and 8-9 open positions for the second decade. There are currently a couple uncovered cargoes available, with the latest deals closing around mid to mid/high 120 H/C range.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: AMERICAS Terminal fee levels for 2H April and 1H May are pretty firmly entrenched at the 7cpg level – the rate at which a series of transactions are known to have occurred within that timeframe.  The 2H May market ranges a bit more widely as buyers and sellers ideas diverge – but only by a half-cent, or so.  The EIA propane inventory data for the week ending 05 April 2024 was generally anticipated to reveal a build of a half-million or so barrels of propane – which would have brought overall stocks well in to the 52mmbbl range.  However, a draw of 100,000bbls was recorded and stock levels now stand at 51.7mmbbls.   Not only did the overall total raise a few eyebrows, but a secondary surprise was noted with a 600,000bbl build on the Gulf Coast in PADD III.  Exports have been extremely robust and so to see a build is noteworthy.  From the higher vantage point, US propane stocks at the first week of October have ranged anywhere from 90-102mmbbls as of the first week of October.  This year should see little difference, as current calculations put the first-week Oct inventory level at between 94-98mmbbls … “right down the fairway”, as it is said.  NWE Competing factors have left participants puzzled when trying to conceive direction in the European LPG market- Following a month of seemingly unworkable arbitrage econs (US /NWE) already 430,000 tons have pointed toward NWE  from various US export terminals, which, given warm weather and balanced stocks, would cover any and all demand. However, Propane remains the preferred feedstock to Naphta,  both of which are off around  $10 from their April high’s. Scheduled  maintenance  at Karsto (April 12-18) and Mongstad (April 5-17), further compounded by an unplanned outage in the run up, will likely cause a disruption of north sea supplied LPG supplied to NWE, all of which could theoretically leave NWE LPG tighter than appears.

The Panamax market has exhibited signs of struggle across various regions. Despite an uptick in ECSA grain shipments hinting at a possible market rebound, the immediate outlook remains subdued. In the Atlantic, a significant lack of fresh demand against a backdrop of increasing tonnage has kept the market under pressure, with rates continuing to be affected negatively. The situation is further exacerbated by a correction in the BPI timecharter average and a distinct absence of activity, particularly in the North Atlantic. Similarly, the Asian market faces challenges due to a lack of new demand and the impact of holidays, contributing to a pessimistic sentiment. Despite some isolated discussions of steadier rates for deferred dates, the Panamax market is currently characterized by low activity, an oversupply of tonnage, and a cautious market sentiment.

Eid celebrations have slowed down activity as many people are enjoying holidays around the world, causing a slight softening on spot rates. Vessel availability has increased on the prompt, as ample sublet tonnage is being pushed into the market, coupled with independent owners’ tonnage redeliveries from their previous term charters. More requirements are expected to emerge for May cargoes next week and this should see tonnage being absorbed.  On the term side, Charterers interest has turned to multimonth terms covering summer as well as for autumn and into winter and periods discussed are around a year, but the bid/ ask spread is still a little wide for now. There were no newbuild orders reported this week. Prices at the yards remain stable, with activity mainly for larger tankers.

Seasonality suggests the market will bottom here and rise slowly the next couple of months. Fundamentals are supportive, with shipment volume growth above the rate of supply growth. Industrial metals prices (copper, aluminum, zinc, and nickel) are rising, suggesting firming global industrial activity. Industrial metals prices often lead the Supra/Ultra (as well as Panamax/Kamsarmax and Handysize) market by 4-6 months. The lead points upwards going forward.

A quiet week for the VLCCs as a lot of under the radar activity have resulted in TD3C sliding 3-4 points from WS 66.15 to WS 62.70. Charterers have done well in keeping a lid on the requirements being worked as owners have been satisfied with fixing last done, or slightly less depending on the voyage/counterpart/terms. The April MEG count lacking about 20 cargoes or so to compare with the last couple of months, and the tonnage list should be more than enough stacked to absorb the remaining stems for April. Quiet in the market at the time of writing with Korea, Singapore, and Middle East off due to Eid celebrations. There are though a ‘pick up’ in activity on the smaller sizes in the West, and owners with ships in the Atlantic hoping it will spill over to the bigger sisters.

On the C5 front, we see a moderate level of volumes from miners, some operators, and tenders all primarily for late April dates. Limited enquiries from some operators for forward May dates. Volumes out of East Australia and other Pacific businesses have picked up, with enquiries ranging from second half of April prompt dates till mid May dates. Volumes out of South Africa have remained flat from last week. On C3 ex Brazil to China and West Africa, volume of enquiries has maintained from last week with majority for May dates. Far East tonnage is increasingly abundant. Ballasting tonnage weighs heavily on first half of May with some vessels drifting off South Africa able to make second half of April dates. On C5, we see a pullback from last week with fixtures concluding at sub USD 9 pmt levels. On C3, we see fixtures concluding at mid USD 24 pmt levels for mid-May.

The North Sea market has been steady for the last week, but with US and Mediterranean markets firming rapidly this week the sentiment is now on the firmer side.  Date wise we are moving into the 3rd decade. With surrounding markets providing better returns we will see vessels ballast out of the area putting pressure on the available tonnage. Some sustained demand is needed to crystalize the firmer sentiment.  The 2nd decade has proven busier than expected in the Mediterranean and coinciding with surrounding areas that are also under pressure, rates have improved. Rates reached the equivalent of Suezmaxes which are also under upward pressure and cargoes restricted to only Aframax struggle as owners made their sentiment clear. Delays in Trieste and Fos are expected to push vessels further back, but vessels from the UKC will be there to make their move into the Mediterranean.

US Gulf Aframax's are the gift that keeps on giving (to owners at least) and are the key support mechanism for Suezmax with rates in the wider Atlantic, benefiting from the US Gulf's unique microclimate (the tail is well and truly wagging the dog). Thanks to activity across the pond TD 20 has up-ticked 12.5 points in the last forty-eight hours to WS 120 with no downside.  There is no evident butterfly effect from the Atlantic into the Far East (for now) where miserly enquiry levels will keep MEG/East rates pinned down at WS 115-120 whilst BOT/UKCM should trade conference WS 67.5. We repeat are call from previous updates that with fewer ships performing West/East moves, there will be a crunch time in the offing where the supply of ships becomes very low by historical comparison, but that is a little further down the line.

The start to Q2 has been somewhat disrupted with various holidays, however, it is not expected that it will mirror the explosive Q1 in the dry market. Asset prices rose sharply as buyers looked to acquire prompt market ships to take advantage of increasing rates, even enticing non-traditional dry players into the space. This sentiment appears to have shifted as those buyers who missed out on the rush have either been priced out, or indeed have turned to sellers themselves to try and capitalise on the inflated values. One could fall back on the underlying overall vessel supply argument, but it just feels that buyers are not comfortable at the current market levels, hence the downtick in sales. In the modern Ultramax space WORLD ROYAL (61K DWT DACKS 2022) sold for USD 35M, while NEW CHAMP (66K DWT MITSUI TAMANO 2018) was bought by Meghna for USD 33.85M.   The reinvestment focus of the tanker market continues to be in Newbuildings, as the number of second-hand transactions stutters. In a rare modern tanker transaction, scrubber fitted Aframax AURVIKEN (112K DWT SAMSUNG HI 2019) was auctioned off and eventually sold to Greek buyers for USD 73M, this auction was a result of part of the ownership structure making the unit subject to sanctions against Russia. Elsewhere, Minerva offloaded Ice 1c MINERVA HELEN (103K DWT SAMSUNG HI 2004) for USD 30.35M.

text: MEG Saudi Aramco set Apr CP at $615 for C3 and $620 for C4, down by $15 and $20 respectively, which is lower than expectation, partly owing to the spot availability on FOB cargos. KPC was reported to sell two evenly split cargos recent, with one for 14/15 Apr prompt loading at CP minus 50s and the other at minus 20s for a later laycan. Qatar Petroleum released May lifting schedule with no cuts but some minor delays.   FAR EAST A handful of deals concluded in window this week. 46/0 for 2h May delivery was changed hand at Bal Apr FEI minus $7 which equates to May FEI plus mid-single digit on the date. 11/11 and 0/23 for same period delivery were concluded at May FEI plus $6.9. 46/0 for 1h May delivery was bid at May FEI plus $11 basis Yantai and 23/0 parcel for 2h May delivery bid at $7 but few offers seen in window.   Before the Qingming festival, a flurry of tenders was awarded this week. Taiwan FPC was reported to award two full propane cargos at May MOPJ minus high 60s into Mailiao and May FEI plus high teens into Ningbo via tenders. Another three Chinese petchem players also awarded 23/0 parcels at May FEI (or mix of May and Jun FEI) plus low-mid teens respectively, for prompt 2h Apr to 1h May delivery. Apart from propane, one SChina traditional player also tendered to buy 11/11 for 1-20 May delivery but was reported cancelled. However, one Iranian origin 3/1 cargo for late Apr delivery was placed into China at May CP plus $10 reportedly. HTC also tendered to buy 23kt butane for 10-19 May delivery.

EAST US freight came up slightly this week while levels in the Middle East was moving in the opposite direction. Availability in the East generally looks longer than in the West, but with many of the end April vessels in the MEG also appearing on the West list we could possibly see some of them seek cargoes in the US. A total of 22 spot fixtures have so far been fixed in the Middle East on April dates versus an average so far this year at 23 (April last year we counted 25 spot deals on April dates ex MEG and Yanbu).  WEST Fixing in the Western hemisphere looks to be more or less finished for April dates, counting 32 spot deals out of the US. For May we have already seen a few fixtures done and there are currently several players out looking for freight in the first half of the month. The vessel supply for first decade May is looking relatively tight seeing 5-6 available positions - half of them being relets. We see the tightness continue into the second decade as we find last done fixture concluded for May dates at mid 120s H/C.

text: AMERICAS Domestic US propane inventory expectations for the week ending 29 March ranged from a draw of around a half-million barrels to as much as a build of over a million barrels.  On yesterday the EIA reported a 400,000bbl decline in stocks which brought the overall total to 51.80mmbbls.  This is 93% of last year, but 150% of two years ago.  One of the components to the Mont Belvieu pricing structure – and one of the several reasons that the MB complex has retained it strength – is the concern that robust exports would limit the ability of domestic stocks to reach suitable levels later in the Fall.  However, calculations are presently indicating that stock levels will – in the first week of October – range somewhere between 94-98mmbbls which is well within the comfort zone.  Nonetheless, MB propane has enjoyed the support from the crude arena, which from the front of March to now has increased by $5/bbl (and rising).   The fact that domestic US crude inventories rose by 3.2mmbbls last week has had little (or no) impact, as geopolitical concerns continue to apply upward pressure.  With regards the US terminal fees, a couple of transactions were noted for end-Apr and (separately) early-May, each at 7cpg.  A couple of other parcels are on offer in the first decade of May in the low 7cpg range, with buy-side interest beginning to collect in the upper 6cpg range.

The West/East arb' is narrow at best and remains in steep backwardation, suggesting that intra-Atlantic trades are likely to benefit Suezmax in the short/medium term. On that front, USG/TA has just traded up, with last done posting WS 82.5 which will act as a support mechanism for the wider Atlantic market.  In the East, there has been a trickle of activity with BOT/UKCM trading conference at WS 67.5 with no obvious downside. MEG/East remains around the WS 120 level and if owners start to examine the list closely they will see that at first glance it looks rather long, but upon further inspection, the ships are in the hands of fewer participants than usual.

The seasonal trend indicates that the index’s peak of USD 21,000 per day is unlikely to be surpassed until June, due to notable slowdowns in major trades and limited optimism for an uptick in Pacific coal trades or a surge in ECSAM grain season. The period following the holiday weekend started quietly, with stagnant Atlantic conditions and surplus tonnage driving rates down. Market activity has been muted, with low cargo volumes contributing to increased tonnage availability and a pessimistic market outlook.

Following recent softening, rates have stabilised in the spot and period markets as national holidays globally have limited levels of activity. The main source of requirements has arisen from market cargo tenders across all basins that seek vessels subject to award, yet most of these opportunities are being covered through portfolios with available tonnage to utilise.  A consequence is that prompt availability remains well stocked, yet owners are unwilling to lock in a large idle periods at current levels, and with most requirements a few weeks out, the misalignment is causing protracted negotiations.    From the yards, four newbuilding's confirmed this week with a JV between K Line and Hyundai Glovis being awarded part of the QE Phase 2 requirement. Delivery August 2027 and a price in the region of $230M USD. For unallocated slots, prices remain flat. The second-hand market also continues to be active with robust prices as further sales are reported this week, although the details of these sales consisting of two mid-size carriers is not yet fully known.

Due to the Easter holiday across Europe, we see significantly reduced trading activity. It’s a little to report. In the Atlantic, most regions remained quiet with little volume; rates continued to fall. The reduced demand from the US Gulf and ECSA as the main loading area caused significant rate drops. Trips from Brazil to Asia are being reported to be fixed at around USD 17,000 pd plus USD 675,000 gross BB, which is substantially lower than the fixtures done before Easter.   Transatlantic is now trading at around USD 18,000 pd. A similar situation in the Pacific, as the lack of recovery in coal shipments is limiting further gains. Pacific China round trips fixing sub USD 15,000 pd.  Period activity is almost non-existent due to the recent FFA drop, and charterers is looking for the future direction.

A fair volume of pre-Easter fixing covered a lot of the first decade. Tonnage list remains balanced with a tight shuttle market and vessels still ballasting away. Interest from owners depends on cargo specifics with other regions providing better alternatives. Market feels like it may have bottomed out, increased demand will absorb the supply of tonnage and start to support rates.  Mediterranean market has been busy as charterers looked to cover Libya stems up to mid-month, whilst Ceyhan and CPC push to finish 2nd decade of April stems. Shaky itineraries and a busy fixing window kept owners excited with some inflated replacement rates, though Suezmaxes lacking conviction in the area could take the edge off. Tonnage looks sensible with inquiring ballasters from the North looking to engage with Mediterranean stems.

On the C5 front, albeit a slight drop in overall volumes compared to last week, enquiries are still present from miners, several operators, and tenders for mid to late April dates. Limited enquiries for forward May dates. Volumes out of East Australia and other Pacific business have diminished since start of the week. Volumes out of South Africa have remained flat from last week. On C3 ex Brazil to China and West Africa, volume of enquiries has maintained from last week with majority for May dates and several for late April. Far East tonnage is increasingly abundant. Ballasting tonnage weighs heavily on the second half of April and first half of May with some drifting off South Africa able to make first half of April dates. On C5, the week started with fixtures concluding at mid USD 9 pmt levels and we noticed a tick increase to high USD 9 pmt levels by mid-week. On C3, we see offers in the range of USD 25 to USD 26 pmt levels with bid ideas in the USD 23 to USD 24 pmt levels for first half of May dates. One known fixture of a 180k dwt, 2011-built, non-scrubbered for 10 to 12 months at USD 30,150 per day.

If not a resurrection, the market showed signs of improvement as the trading week kicked off. Whilst most of the Western world were still stuffing their face with Easter eggs Monday saw a couple of MEG/East concluded at higher numbers. Extrapolating on the last couple of months we might have another 3-5 cargoes left to be covered for 2nd decade April in the MEG but barring some Chinese Uber bookings the third decade has hardly been touched, and there’s only the balance of this week and next week to cover it before we start to see May stems emerging. The front end of the MEG position list is also well balanced, if not tight. However, Atlantic action has been wanting and the position list has been added to by Venezuelan stems evaporating. USG export is also behind the curve and downward pressure appears inevitable unless activity picks up.

As we approach the end of the first quarter, the market can reflect on a very busy few months in which players have adapted well to the changing dynamics. With both canals essentially out of action, with the implementation of the EU ETS scheme, with engine power limitation restricting some speeds and with LNG supply surges and disruptions, there has been a lot to deal with! Perhaps unsurprisingly given these uncertainties, the LNG freight market did not drop as fast or as far as some had predicted, and the past weeks had seen a broadly flat market with spot rates for 2-strokes staying above the $50k per day mark; however, ongoing LNG production issues and vessel over-supply are now weighing on rates, and this important benchmark has been breached. There continues to be enough demand to keep owners and sub-letters busy and there is life in the arbitrage for US Gulf cargoes to go East, although many of the emerging requirements are tenders or optimisations and the spot market is now softening. On multi-month and longer term charters, there has been a slight lull as owners and charterers are a little out of alignment on periods and rates right now, but this is temporary and activity will pick up again as we approach the summer months. There have been no new orders this week.

A short week which will be mostly remembered for... Sorry, let me start again. This week will likely not be remembered in Suezmax history. On the large part rates have stayed where they were on Monday. Most the fixing has been off market. Med suezmaxes are being propped up by Aframax cargoes but even those rates are under pressure. W.Africa has threatened to notch up since 130 x w110 has been done for TD20 but hasn't yet. Really it should do but there's enough early tonnage which hasn't managed to find an employer. Guyana/Ukcm fixed at 145 x w92.5 - this was more than expected with the reason being that any USG-USAC or ECC position is likely to favour Usg/Ukcm at 145 x w75. This leaves the Guyana cargoes to look at Cont/W.Med ballasters only. The MEG has seen a bit of activity today after nothing all week. But really it's been flat before the weekend and W.Africa/MEG will probably tick up a touch but it's been largely uneventful. The good news is, Suezmaxes have flatlined since mid-January and these are still good earnings for Owners.

NSEA: Market has seen some activity the last couple of days with rates moving sideways. North Sea crude stems look to be almost covered for at least the first 5 days of April and with relets/  Vlcc’s and Suezmax in the equation probably  closer to the 10th. This could leave the market lacking in opportunity up to the end of the first decade. Surrounding markets still attractive to ballast out of the North but the volume ballasting has petered somewhat.  MED: Rates steady/softer even with some pre-Easter long weekend activity as Charterers worked ahead to fill their programmes. Early Libyan stems are slight for 1st decade April already jumping toward mid-first decade dates whilst Ceyhan and CPC push on in to the second decade fixing window. A good number of units scheduled to discharge end/ely in this region so come next week there is potential for some downward pressure on rates.

A week of dropping rates, but likely the bottom now and the green shoots of recovery already evident. The usual suspects S-Oil fixing the lowest point on a Worldscale basis (in the ws50’s), but in the face of a quiet market, Owners have been able to maintain rates in the ws60’s. I say quiet, but on the surface only, as it is clear the vast majority of deals done quietly and kept under the radar to not jeopardise subs in a falling market. The problem with this tactic is the lists look artificially long and the market suffers further. But now, with a tighter list and most 10-20 April cargoes still to work, Owners should be able to push the rates back up through the ws60’s. The Atlantic usually leads the recovery charge, but it has been quiet with several early ships and therefore little desire for Owners to ballast that way. However, we are likely as low as we will see, with USG/Ningbo rates $8.75m level to test.

After the furore of the last few weeks, it seems as though the dry market has taken somewhat of a breather. Small and medium sized buyers are looking at the market more tentatively than before, having seen price expectations on units increase rapidly over the last quarter. Earnings stuttered this week, reminding buyers that everything can change quickly. Capes are still receiving healthy premiums, with ORANGE TIARA 181K DWT KOYO 2012 selling at USD 35M, exceeding what was paid for 1-year younger KINOKAWA MARU 181K DWT IMABARI 2013 (USD 34M) back in February. Supramax STRAITS BAY 55K DWT KAWASAKI 2007 sold for a very sizeable USD 14.75M, showing the premium buyers would pay for a very prompt ship. Elsewhere Lauritzen sold scrubber fitted handy bc ASIAN BULKER 36K DWT SHIKOKU DOCKYARD 2017 for USD 24M.   It was a fairly lacklustre week in the tanker market, despite a jump in earnings. Modern second hand tonnage is still hard to come by, with the majority of activity happening on the newbuilding front. In the notable transaction for the week, Scorpio sold MR pair STI LE ROCHER/STI LARVOTTO 49K DWT HMD 2013 for USD 36.2M each.

EAST The East has been quiet this week with only one spot fixture registered, and in total we now count 8 deals for April dates ex MEG. 7 of these have been done 1-10 April which is one above the average for the first decade the last three months. There are currently no signs of Indian PSUs in April just yet – which quoted 7 cargoes in March. With earnings in the West weakening lately, meaning less incentive to sail that direction, we could see more ships considering going East.  WEST After a rush of deals in the West last week, we have only seen one spot deal this week and it was concluded 13-14 dollars lower than last done. Currently we count 26 spot fixtures for April ex USG/USEC and we still see about 10 vessels open that month – the majority of them in the last decade. At the same time there are still half a dozen uncovered cargoes left for end April dates.

text: AMERICAS Mont Belvieu propane values, which remain remarkably resilient, continue to be buoyed by gains being recorded in the crude arena, and which thus have allowed propane prices to continue on an upward trajectory.  This is despite reduced weather-related demand across North America, effectively flat petrochemical demand, as well as the relationship to crude (which presently stands at ~41%), and that stock levels are not only sufficient, but are presently calculated to rise to the mid 90mmbbl level by around the first week of October.  Indeed the weekly export volumes have been robust, but on balance – and over the coming inventory build season - there is not a tremendous amount of upside to existing capacity levels.  Of course the lifting of the daylight restrictions on the HSC has had a positive impact, but some of those efficiency gains are lost to the regular calling of larger and larger VLGCs.  Meanwhile, the EIA yesterday reported a nearly flat (+300k bbls) propane stock level for the week ending 15 March, bringing total overall primary inventories in the U.S. to 52.2mmbbls.  This is 89% of the total recorded a year ago, and 155% of the total seen two years ago.  If only average weekly gains are achieved over the course of the next 6+ months, a ~95mmbbl inventory level will have been achieved.  Despite periodic arguments to the contrary, all signs point to a normal build season.  As for the current spot market, the March program is effectively concluded though a handful of parcels remain on offer in April – mostly at around the 8cpg level.  May cargoes and demand levels are beginning to be revealed, but terminal fees are expected to be a penny or so lower.

The Panamax market has seen divided opinions recently, with the BPI timecharter average slightly up but facing skepticism over its peak, amid a backdrop of a weakening FFA market leading to stand-offs. Despite a subdued start to the week, positive sentiment persists, supported by stable fundamentals across both Atlantic and Asian regions, suggesting potential for future gains. The market is closely watching cargo flow and tonnage availability, crucial for maintaining or improving rate levels, amidst a cautious approach from charterers in response to mixed market signals and firm levels in areas like ECSA.

West Africa, busy week so far, April stems in play with questions on the Nigerian Freight Tax waver coming to an end, which helped rates push slightly higher. Tonnage is a little tighter off the beginning of the month but suspect the market to won't change a great deal going forward.   The Mediterranean-Black Sea, once again all about the Aframax market which remained firm and helped the Suezmax market maintain last done levels from the Black Sea, with the Mediterranean seeing Suezmax vessels covering Aframax cargoes at 80k at WS 170.  US Gulf revolved around the Aframax market once again with market looking softer, understand last done was 145k at WS 82.5, whilst we saw better rate levels covered from Guyana with increased activity helped by the West Africa market, rates running in at 145k at WS 90 for UKCM by mid-week.  The Middle East Gulf, busy start to the week with plenty of action enabling the rates to climb to WS 67.5 for Basrah/UKCM via Cape, little activity East but rates should be around the WS 122.5 for Eastern destinations for modern tonnage.

On the C5 front, we see a reasonably healthy volume of enquiries from miners for early April dates and operators from early to mid April dates. Several were seen for second half of April and forward May dates. In comparison, things were quiet on the East Australia coal front at the beginning of the week but gradually picked up as we approach mid-week. Volumes on other Pacific business and South Africa remained flat from last week. On C3 ex Brazil to China and West Africa, we see enquiries primarily for second half of April. Tonnage in Far East remains moderately tight. Ballasting tonnage weighs heavily on April with seemingly few ships left for late March. On C5, we observe the same trend as last week; starting off with fixtures concluding at USD 13 pmt levels and retreating to high USD 11 pmt levels by mid-week. On C3, we see fixtures concluding at USD 28 to USD 29 pmt levels for second half of April dates.

A very sluggish start to the MEG April program has seen a tonnage buildup, with vessels sailing free of cargo in the East. Coupled with a number of relets, and the scene is set for a rate drop. At the time of writing, one Thailand bound cargo has attracted a reported 10 offers showing the lack of choice available to the build-up of tonnage. Rates will come off, but TCE’s are still very attractive and there is no shame for owners fixing on vessels date at a good level. Cargo wise, we are behind schedule and the bulk of early April will come eventually, but with each passing (quiet) day, that MEG list lengthens.  The Atlantic market was saddened at the news of a failure ex USG/Ningbo at USD 9.55m, a decent number, but the 2024 USG/Ningbo average so far stands at USD 9.2m, and if stretched too far above that, it would appear subs can become trickier.   Softer overall, but fundamentals are there to prevent the falling off a cliff… the power is in the owners’ (and Oil Co. relets) hands.

The Pacific and Indian Ocean: On Supra/Ultra sizes, we see lower volumes in terms of cargo in the market. NOPAC RV being done at mid USD 13,000 levels and backhaul trips being priced at around USD 11,000 levels. Meantime on the MEG-India side, the usual WCI-China trips being fixed at USD 17/18,000 levels and inter-MEG trips being done at USD 16,000 mark. Backhaul trips being done at USD 7,000 levels on Supramax.   The Atlantic markets: The USG market remains firm cue the low tonnage count and increased cargo volume. TA being fixed around mid USD 15,000 levels and fronthaul voyages being done tick over USD 20,000 mark. On the ECSA side, tonnage availability remains tight and trips to Far East being done at high USD 20,000 levels whereas TA trips being done at USD 20,000 levels.     The market on Handy remains firm with ECSA - fronthaul trips being done at USD 24,000 levels and transatlantic trips paying around USD 20,000.   With only 3 months to go for the monsoon season to start in India, we can expect to see less activity on the iron biz from WCI in the coming months and ships being repositioned accordingly. On the other hand, there is still potential for an upside in the Atlantic given the ECSA grain season is not yet at peak levels. Meantime, period market remains active with couple fixtures reported this week. Healthy rates and activity in the Atlantic overall. However, as they say ‘Every storm runs out of rain eventually, even a “perfect” one, but the forecast for markets next week is likely more of the same.

The North Sea has seen very limited activity in the first half of the week.  Early tonnage availability has been reduced with vessels ballasting initially towards US, but with market softening in the US tonnage has been turning towards a firmer Mediterranean market. Rates in the region have remained steady and dates now pushing into the last 5 days of the month. Local tonnage should recycle towards the end of the month and be supplemented with tonnage arriving into the area.  Activity in the Mediterranean this week has seen owners test the limits on end month March stems whilst trying to compete with Suezmax for employment. Tighter tonnage off the front end has allowed owners to be bullish on rates, but with Suezmax there to intervene on a level footing and a projected replenishment of tonnage for April dates, ships opening in the area should help to ease the pressure on charterers and steady the market as we move forward.

As we approach the end of Q1 2024, the LNG shipping market maintains a steady course, a typical scenario for this time of year characterized by lower demand and moderated LNG prices. There is some uncertainty on the cargo side, with traders keeping a close eye on supply concerns such from potential cyclone disruptions in Australia, unplanned maintenance of Norway’s Aasta gas field and some lower production out of Nigeria.   In spite of the above, there have been signs of a reviving freight market with several requirements firming up in both basins and firming rates for modern tonnage in the Atlantic. The first half of this week saw some anticipated spot requirements firm up in the East, accompanied by a couple of new opportunities for tonnage holders out of the Atlantic. With the high vessel competition in the east, owners and charterers will be keen to see how rates will move in the wake of this activity. Furthermore, although cargoes have been traded within their respective basins, there is a small arbitrage flickering to life and charterers are seeking flexibility to head East. As well as increased spot activity, multi month and term business continues to be discussed although the specific periods being sought by charterers or offered by owners are not always aligned.   There were no newbuilding orders reported this week; however, prices remain stable.

There is a feeling of the second-hand S&P market resembling a runaway train, particularly on dry, where we see huge activity at rapidly firming levels. Modern tonnage is still hard to come by, however, over the next few months owners may find the surging prices too much to resist provided the market is willing to pay up. Scrubber fitted Newcastlemax sisters ATLANTIC TIGER/DRAGON 209K DWT SWS 2020 fetched a notable USD 71M per vessel to Pan Ocean. A rally  in values that becomes particularly apparent when compared to the USD 63.5M per vessel paid for scrubber fitted BULK SHANGHAI/SEOUL 208K DWT NEW TIMES 2019 in February of this year. Otherwise, players have been jostling for older units where competition is quickly driving up prices and expectations. There were 10 buyers on supramax QUEEN BUSAN 55K DWT KAWASAKI HI 2010, which eventually sold at USD 17.15M, setting a new benchmark in this competitive size and age bracket.  The tanker market of late has been somewhat flying under the radar, rates have remained firm with a high level of purchase enquiry that is met short by an ever-thinning list of available candidates . In the immediate term, appetite is slightly lower on older units, perhaps due to some scepticism over sanctions and longevity of this run. That said, Turkish buyers are reported to have picked up suezmax KARVOUNIS 156K DWT SUMITOMO 2013 at 67.5M. Elsewhere, older units have softened, seen in scrubber fitted VLCC ACHELOUS 299K DWT IHI 2004 at USD 30M (SS due 09/24).

EAST While there remains a considerable number of vessels potentially available for first decade April dates in the Middle East, the active West market and the uncertainty surrounding many ships' itineraries have contributed to propelling the East market to new heights. Presently, we have tallied five spot fixtures scheduled within the first decade of April, with pending acceptances from Aramco yet to be received and no signs of Indian PSUs just yet. Overall, the market sentiment remains strong.  WEST The Western market has been red hot this week with close to 20 spot fixtures done out of the USG and freight rates have now risen to mid/high 130s H/C and mid/high 70s H/F. The vessel supply for the rest of April is looking balanced to tight, but we find most of the ships open in the last decade of the month where we so far only have seen 6 spot fixtures. We expect more cargoes to appear as we so far count 25 deals for April dates ex USG/USEC.

text: MEG Discussions for evenly split cargos declined further with one Apr lifting FOB changed hand at Apr CP minus $20s. Similar parcel was offered in window this Thur at Apr CP minus $22. One India major tendered to buy such cargo, which is expected to get very aggressive offers.   At the time of writing, Apr C3 CP was traded at $604 and C4/C3 narrowed to $2 amid ample butane supply. Apr/May C3 CP was traded at $30 backwardation.    FAR EAST Bids for 23/0 1h Apr delivery edged up to Apr FEI plus $18 in window, and similar cargo for 2h Apr also improved to teens level with one concluded at Apr FEI plus $13.5. Off window 46/0 2h Apr basis Chiba was rumored traded at Apr FEI plus mid-single digit. With stronger bids and higher freight, Apr FEI/CP swung from -$15 to $2.   Before upcoming China conference, several petchem players have called tenders to secure feedstock for Apr delivery. One North China PDH user was reported to buy a 1h Apr delivered 46/0 at Apr FEI plus low teens via tender. One EChina PDH user didn’t award their Apr procurement tender due to potential turnaround for PDH operation reportedly. One EChina cracker user issued tender to buy a 46/0 for mid Apr delivery into Ningbo, which is in validity.   Other than propane, a couple of butane buying tenders floating in the market. One SChina cracker was reported to cancel their tender for Apr delivery LPG and ended up buying special origin cargo. And CPC tendered to buy 11/11 for last decade Apr delivery. One Japanese importer also was reported to procure 0/23 or 11.5/11.5 or 0/11.5 for April arrival via tender.

The market remains active in most sectors with rates holding steady overall so far this week. West Africa as we have said has seen under the radar fixing recently but again not enough market cargoes being seen working to build momentum and sentiment for the owners. Rates we suspect should still be around the WS 105-107.5 level for UKCM.  The Mediterranean/Black Sea region is ticking over, but the Aframax market which has been helping hold up the rate levels, did slow down with only a few cargoes in the market. We are going to need more enquiry to keep at the last done levels in the Suezmax market off natural dates. We saw a Hariga to Ningbo voyage cover at USD 5.3m via Cape, which we think was lower than most owners would have considered. The Black Sea saw the end of the third decade working with rates fixing upto WS 107.5 for min flat Augusta, with a few Suezmax units covering Aframax parcels. Delays still are minimal for the Turkish Straits and is still tonnage in good supply.   US Gulf has been ticking over with a West Coast India run covering at USD 5.4m, whilst T/A voyages maintaining WS 100.   Middle East Gulf has been busy, with one charterer reaching out to April dates for a MEG/East which is reported to have covered. Likely in the WS 120 levels for East, if modern, although we’ve hardly seen any activity from Basrah but a few Kuwait fuel tenders working, whilst we saw one vessel fail STS Kaz to the US Gulf allegedly at USD 4.1m. Sentiment is flat here in the MEG.

The market started stabilizing in a positive direction. Demand increased in the USG and ECSA , where the Panamax stems were decreased in size and fixed on Ultra. We see a good number of fresh cargoes for Atlantic trade.    Fronthaul from USG to Singapore-Japan was covered at USD 24,000 pd. Transatlantic trips from USG and NCSA to Mediterranean were reported to be fixed at USD 14,000 pd, and to the Continent at USD 15,000 pd.  The Continent and Mediterranean markets also improved in better rates, and some healthy fixtures were reported. Ultra 63,000 dwt was fixed for scrap to East Mediterranean at USD 18,000 pd.  Russian fertilizers from Baltic to Morocco are fixed at USD 25,000 pd on Ultramax, and Supra to USG from Ust Luga at USD 17,000 pd. India Ocean and South Africa were stable, and rates kept a firm pace.   The Pacific market was increasing in most routes and charterers were willing to pay better than last done by more than USD 1,000 pd. Supra dely Vietnam was reported at USD 15,000 pd for a trip with coal to South East Asia, while another 55,000 dwt with dely South China fixed at USD 16,000 pd for a trip via Indonesia to EC India. The market has a firm undertone, and we believe it will continue to be so in the coming weeks.

The North Sea from end of last week into this week has seen consistent enquiry pushing dates into 3rd decade.  An active fuel oil market taking vessels out of the area either T/A or into the Red Sea, combined with a continued stream of ballasters has depleted the early tonnage but natural tonnage turning around and tonnage coming into the area should repopulate the list into the end 3rd decade.  Firmer sentiment.  Upward pressure to the Mediterranean Aframax market this week. A subdued, steadier feel in the first half was eclipsed as rates jumped mid-week with fixing window pushing out to end month for East Mediterranean cargoes and last 5 days in North Africa.  Further pressure on tonnage and rates in the short term but a steady turn-around of vessels should replenish list heading into April.

The Panamax market has seen a significant increase, mainly in the Atlantic due to a shortage of ships and strong demand, primarily from the North Atlantic and East Coast South America (ECSA), driving rates up. The Panamax Timecharter Average (P5TC) rose to USD 18,353, reflecting this positive trend. Although Asia's market started slowly, it remained stable, supported by reliable demand and the recent surge from ECSA, maintaining a positive outlook despite limited visibility. The market demonstrated resilience with increased grain inquiries and expectations for further gains, particularly in the Atlantic, buoyed by firm demand and lower tonnage availability. The week started slowly but maintained a strong sentiment, with the market responding positively to the Atlantic and Pacific dynamics, indicating sustained strength and confidence in future performance.

On the C5 front, we see a reasonably healthy volume of enquiries from miners, operators, and tenders primarily for first half of April, and limited volume for late March and forward May to June dates. In comparison, things are relatively quieter on the East Australia coal front. Enquiries in other Pacific regions started off quiet in the week but soon picked up by mid-week. Volumes on South African business remains relatively flat. On C3 ex Brazil to China and West Africa, enquires are primarily for April and forward May dates. Tonnage in the Far East remains moderately tight. Ballasting tonnage is relatively tight for late March and first half of April. On C5, the week started off strong with fixtures concluding at USD 13 pmt levels, retreating to mid-high USD 12 pmt levels by mid-week. On C3, we see fixtures concluding at USD high 28 to mid 29 pmt levels for early April dates. One known fixture of a 180k dwt, 2016-built, scrubbered for 12 months at USD 35,000 per day.

After a volatile February, the shipping market has shown signs of stabilization in recent weeks. Both the Atlantic and Asia regions are experiencing a slowdown in spot market activity, with rates holding steady. However, it's important to note that availability continues to increase during this time of year.  In terms of the cargo market, we've observed a softening in TTF prices, with European storage remaining well above the average for this time of year, while JKM prices have seen an increase relative to TTF.,  This has presented some limited opportunities for an inter-basin arbitrage and as a result, we have seen several cargoes heading east. Given the availability lists, this dynamic hasn’t stressed the freight market yet, but may help explain the steady charter rates.  Market activity continues to lean towards more multi-month requirements, although levels are remaining steady in this segment, too. There haven’t been any fresh newbuilding orders placed this week.

MEG March stem volume will close out this week at around 145 total cargoes. Likely a very brief lull before the April cargoes start working (although we have already seen a 1-2/Apr Al Shaheen Smax stem and some Chinese to Chinese business off April dates already). The early birds may start working at the end this week, early next, so rates likely a flat in the MEG for the time being at the WS 70 level. We count 30 vessels on the water, free of cargo at present, so the list is lengthening a touch.   A little different in the West however - a touch softer - USD 9m USG/Ningbo levels, but we are behind the curve a little, so we feel a pickup in activity in the next few days. Worth noting the average for 2024 so far USG/Ningbo is USD 9.2m, so it seems owners and charterers seem to have found the happy level that the route works at. West Africa/East done at WS 70, albeit an older vessel.

Lack of liquidity is a distant memory for dry market players as the run on second hand bulkers continues this week. Perhaps a cause for all this excitement is that despite the seemingly buoyant market, there is still some way to go before historical highs are reached, at least from a TC point of view. There is work to be done even to eclipse the 2022 TC market, though judging by the ever-increasing competition on any new market candidate, there is no shortage of confidence that this will not be achieved. Modern Scrubber fitted Tess 82 Kamasarmax SANKO HAWKING 82K DWT TSUNEISH 2021 sold this week at a notable USD 41.5M. At the other end of the age curve where values are likely to fluctuate significantly as players look to take advantage of the spot market, Capesize CASTILLO DE VALVERDE 173K DWT BOHAI 2005 sold at USD 15M.   The second hand wet market is happy to stay out of the headlines this week, with more ink being devoted to the strong demand for Newbuilidng tanker slots. There is still demand for older tankers, albeit softer than we’ve seen in recent times, shown in aframax SEA HAZEL 106K DWT TSUNEISHI TADOTSU 2004 being sold at USD 29M.
