text: AMERICAS The EIA this week revealed its propane inventory data which showed a build of 800,000bbls for an overall total of 102.3mmbbls, or nearly 120% of last year and almost 140% of two years ago.  The 800k bbl increase was not terribly surprising and the market took it in stride since predictions were rather wildly all over the board.  Some were calling for a draw of as much as 800,000bbls, while others were looking for a 3mmbbl build.  In cases when the range of anticipation is so wide it effectively means that the market lacks true confidence, and in this case likely references the past couple of EIA reports which were deemed in need of correction.   Meanwhile, the trio of Force Majeure declarations at the Gulf Coast terminals continues to plague the market, though it is expected at this point that two of the three will shortly be rescinded (if they haven’t been already).  In any case, product availability remains largely limited to re-sellers, many of whom have already committed their volumes.  As such, and based on the current arb, terminal fees remain robust.  Presently the spot FOB terminal fee for propane is pegged at around 13cpg, and for butane at 10cpg.    And while the volatility in the crude arenas – which during October has seen $7/bbl swings - continues to push and pull MB propane values, the ratio of propane to crude continues within a modest range of between 33-35%.  NWE The TOT window has been active this week, without any deals being done. Buying interest for 8-12 November delivery pushed the assessed physical value to a $3/MT premium to November CIF ARA. While the East / West spread has come in to $100/MT for November traders are looking to place VLGCs in the region vs heading East with netback values from the US near parity. LPG imports to the region are expected to be around 550,000MT in October, and although the low demand environment continues imports should increase if netback values remain competitive with the East market. Butane at 79% November Naphtha while demand is increasing due to blending demand and the arrival of colder weather.  MED Suez canal announced it would be increasing transit fees, transit for LPG vessels could rise by 15% beginning January 15th, 2024. Two butane coaster loading from Marcus Hook will be heading to Tunisia, booked when coaster freight was affordable vs larger sized vessels.

EAST As activity gains momentum in both main loading regions ships are gradually disappearing. However, now with 6 confirmed deals in first decade of November and a good handful of vessels still available in the same window, market is still not looking very short in terms of vessels supply. A couple of more cargos could be expected before shifting full focus onto second decade November where we have already seen 3 deals done. With the "cheap options" now taken out Owners ideas are on the rise with last done at mid-low 110s RT/C.  WEST The big jump in Eastern freight has made the premium in the West narrow to approximately 5 dollars before waiting in Panama. Western rates are also on the rise having seen several spot deals done at 180-185 H/C range lately and there should still be a few more deals to be done for November dates, but it remains to be seen if there are enough cargoes left before shifting focus towards December.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG Saudi Aramco released their Nov acceptance and ATC was seen to fix a couple of vessels for Nov liftings, with one heavy butane reported to be placed into India.   A week of volatility in paper swap, following the crude. At the time of writing, Nov C3 CP was traded at $580 and C4 is assessed at $13 higher. Nov/Dec CP was at flattish level. Cash premium for AG evenly split cargos was assessed at teens to $20 level due to the robust demand from India and Indonesia.   FAR EAST Cash differentials for Nov delivered propane softened as of muted discussions. 23kt propane for 2h Nov delivery was offered at Nov FEI minus $3.5 in the window. Outside window, spot inquires remained quiet as petchem importers refrained from buying due to negative margins. Several PDHs were reported to swap or defer their feedstock for Oct delivery to later period.  This being said, one trader issued buy tender to secure a full or heavy propane cargo for late Nov to Dec delivery into Ningbo. Another trader was reported to procure a full propane cargo for 1h Dec delivery into Echina at Dec FEI plus mid single digit.   Unlike propane, demand for evenly split cargos remained strong. One Indian major issued tender to procure two evenly split cargos from Dec to Feb delivery. And PERTAMINA was also reported to secure similar for early Dec arrival.   Other than spot, at least four Chinese Importers have issued term tenders to secure next year’s LPG supply, minimum 2mmt in total. Market players reckoned that it could be a good timing as recent decline in freight might lead to cheaper premium, and which might not sustain for long.

We see healthy volume levels for early November C5, East Australia, and Pacific. On South Africa and Indian business, we see several enquiries from operators for end October to mid November. On C3 ex Brazil to China, volumes are present from miners and operators focusing on early November and mid November respectively. On West Africa, we see several fresh enquiries for mid to late November. On a whole, market optimism remains upbeat. Tonnage is moderately tight on Far East, and we see an uptick in ballasting tonnage. On C5, fixtures concluded at high USD 10 pmt to low USD 11 pmt levels. On C3, fixtures concluded at high USD 26 pmt and high USD 25 pmt levels for early and mid November stems respectively. Big spread for mid November at USD 26 versus USD 27/28 pmt. We see hesitation from owners to match charterer bids and adopting a wait and see approach. One known fixture of a 208k dwt 2010-build non-scrubber delivery China at very end October for about 1 year at low USD 20,000/day.

This has been a big week for the short-term market with a number of fixtures confirming what much of us suspected: there are more bears than bulls in 2024. With competitive one and two-year fixtures on 2-strokes transpiring, the correction has reverberated through the TFDE and ST fleet as well. Paradoxically, the market looks to tighten again as we move out to the three and five year mark, and accordingly the discount that one might expect to see, for these longer periods, has disappeared as the market prices in an uptick in demand from 2026. On the spot side of the house, a rise in LNG prices has helped stem the decline in rates and we are in “wait and see” mode as we go to print today. With most Q4 availability still in the hands of portfolios and projects, current volatility in the product market makes releasing tonnage a risky (i.e., expensive) prospect and it means that closing the Bid-Ask spread into the New Year will remain the biggest challenge. In any event, we have seen a few charterers return to the market for November through to January/February coverage and this may be the precursor for the eventual tightening that we have all come to expect at this time of year. In reality, however, 18th October is way too early to make a call on Winter and the fear is that we remain in our “wait and see” mode indefinitely. To Newbuilds, another quiet week with nothing to report although a number of Majors are heard to be in discussions with the yards, so it may be only a matter of time before we get our next keenly awaited price point here.

To start in the MEG, it’s been a very busy week as the fuel and crude cargoes came thick and fast for end October and early November dates thinning the position list significantly for these dates. TD23 lifted some 10 points or so and is now in the mid 80s, and MEG/East has lifted to the WS 120 mark, some 20 points higher than last week. Moving into the second half of the 1st decade in the MEG, it feels like sentiment should hold, if we see a drop off in activity then expect some downward pressure to start emerging. The Atlantic markets also surged on the back of the Aframax and Suezmax being incredibly busy ex USG. Rates have moved up to WS 117.5 level for TD20 voyages and look to be steadying somewhat as the rush of USG cargoes seems to be slowing down. We don’t expect a huge drop off in levels in West Africa just yet, but it does feel like a small downward correction is likely, given how rapid the rates moved up.

Quite a few owners with vessels open in the North Sea have ballasted away to seek better returns elsewhere on the western hemisphere.  The list has thinned out for normal North Sea candidates, and owners trading in the area have managed to push rates upwards. The firm trend looks to continue into end month October loading dates, and we will see higher than last done be paid this week.   Owners in the Mediterranean/Black Sea market held back last week. Owners pushed the market 80-100 points above last-done levels on the back of a very firm USG market. Tonnage list is slowly starting to balance out a bit and we might see rates finding equilibrium around WS 200 levels now, but the market is still moving. Sentiment is still strong, and owners will try to prevent rates from falling.

As we have seen time and time again, the Atlantic market has been the driver of rates pushing numbers further in to the black for VLCC owners. This week is no different as the benchmark TD22 route pushed up through the 10mill mark. Natural candidates for the mid-November cargoes ex USG remain limited and have helped the other markets rise accordingly. The MEG November program hit the ground running on Monday. The position lists are looking a little more ample later in the month but for very early November, in a word, tight, as owners will make the most of the obtained momentum.  It remains to be seen if owners are able to cling on to current market levels as production cuts are projected for November.

The Panamax market experienced a subdued week, particularly in the Pacific region with minimal activity from North Pacific, Australia, and Indonesia, leading some owners to reposition ships towards the Atlantic. The Atlantic, especially the North Atlantic, observed a better sentiment with a notable increase in transatlantic inquiries and concluded fixtures at improved rates. The spread between Cape and Panamax transatlantic widened, hinting at a spillover from Cape splits to Panamax. However, the fronthaul market remained lackluster, and ECSA spot tonnage offers dipped due to a lack of prompt cargoes. Despite some initial excitement on FFAs, the need for more volume to avoid a further decline was emphasized.

Overall sentiment remained positive in the Atlantic, with rates increasing both in USG and ECSA. Norvic fixed an Ultramax delivery USG with Petcoke to India at USD 31,000 pd. Another 63,000 dwt was fixed at USD 20,000 pd from North Brazil to Mediterranean destination with grain cargo. From South Brazil, 55,000 dwt was fixed at USD 15,000 pd + 550,000 GBB for trip to Asia. Asian arenas remained quiet. A 63,000 dwt delivery China fixed USD 13,500 pd for a trip via Australia to Japan. The South Pacific was holding stable momentum while north for CJK rates started to fall. We expect the market to be volatile with little certainty of direction.

The unfolding geopolitical turmoil in the Middle East is generating headlines and stirring concerns about contagion risks in the region. Although the events haven't yet impacted commodity pricing or shipping rates, the concerns are evident. This week’s Tanker transactions seem like an echo from last week, but this week focused on 15 year old tonnage. We’ve seen the sale of the LR1 CHEMTRANS AEGEAN (76k dwt DALIAN 2007) for $22m and the sale of the MR2 ELIZABETH M (50k dwt SLS 2007) for $22m and MR2 CONSTANCE (50k dwt SPP 2008) for $23.5m.   Although the dry spot market appears to have taken a breather, the secondhand market appears to persist with the volume of transactions. We have recorded the sale of 5 Capesize units built between 2007 and 2010 with pricing pretty much flat from last week demonstrated by the sale of the Capesize AQUA BONANZA (180k dwt IMABARI 2010) sold for $23m. Other noteworthy dry sales are the Ultramax CP SHANGHAI (63k dwt CHENGXI 2015) sold for $23.5m and the Supramax XING HONG DA 8 (58k dwt YANGZHOU DAYANG 2012) sold for $12.7m.

EAST With only two confirmed spot deal on November dates so far and an easing activity level - freight sentiment are currently softening slightly across the board. Aramco acceptances will likely be known by Sunday the earliest and there are talks of some Indian quotes for November dates expected from next week. The East is currently trading at a discount of about 20 dollars according to the latest baltic print.  WEST A small handful of deals have been done in the West this week and we have now count 17 spot fixtures done for November dates ex USG/USEC – for reference the average the last three months have been 32. The position list is still looking balanced to tight seeing only 2 open positions left in the back end of 1H Nov in addition to a vessel in the very end of Oct. For 2H Nov we potentially see 9-10 available positions, but some could end up in MEG and a couple might roll over into December dates.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG ADNOC released their Nov acceptance with some delays reported. Assessment for FOB spot premiums dropped to teens level this week for evenly split ratio. Qatar Petroleum was reported to award a 3/1 ratio for 8-18th Nov lifting at CP plus high single digit. Another Middle east producer is rumored to have mid Nov lifting heavy butane cargo can sell.   At the time of writing, Nov Propane CP was traded at $567 and Butane at $574. Nov/Dec CP was traded at $3 contango.   FAR EAST Premium for Nov delivered cargos softened this week as of subdued buying interests. 23kt propane parcel for 2h Nov delivery were traded at Nov FEI plus $1, while last week at $4.5. Similarly, 46kt propane parcel was reported concluded at Nov FEI minus mid-teens basis Chiba between traders, despite the cargo delays in US loading ports.   Scarce buying demand after holiday also failed the market expectations, as Chinese importers holding back on purchase, due to the negative petchem margins and surplus refinery output. Two PDH users are reported to resell their Oct arrival propane, as their units are under maintenance. Hence, Nov FEI flat price plunged to $638 from $673 on Monday.   Apart from spot, one Korean importer issued term tender to buy monthly 23kt butane from Feb 2024 to Jan 2025 delivery at MOPJ link.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: AMERICAS MB propane values have largely mirrored the movements recorded in the WTI arena, and – as in September - the relationship so far in October has been maintained in the 34% range.  Flat prices, meanwhile, have seen an approximate 5cpg decline since the start of October and now are pegged at 69.00cpg (against a WTI price today of $84.31/bbl).   And after waiting an extra day for the inventory data to be released, the EIA today reported that overall US propane stocks grew by 100,000bbls, which turns out to have been surprising to many since predictions ranged from a -700,000bbl draw to a +1.7mmbbl build.  The EIA also reported an export level of 2.1mmbbls/day, which has also come in to question since several of the LPG marine terminals on the Gulf Coast have been suffering reduced rates which resulted in a trio of Force Majeure declarations.   Terminal fees, all the while, were in decline at the front of the month after having been driven to the mid teens for October business and retreated to buy-side ideas in the upper single digits.  That, however, was replaced by low-teens sell-side ideas for propane, and (at least) double-digits for butane.  NWE The physical window has been more active recently, with an end October TOT offer vs an early November TOT bid, bringing the physical premium to +$2.5/MT to October CIF ARA. Demand in the region is sluggish as petrochemical buying remains low, and is forecast to until mid 2024, while seasonal heating demand is yet to begin. Term imports continue to account for most new demand. While the netback values to the region are still not competitive against heading East. The European market could tighten rapidly as a cold snap heads for the region, while US Gulf loading delays could restrict supply. The butane market have been uneventful, though seasonal demand increase is expected.   MED Warmer than average temperatures in the region have kept demand stagnant. US butane continues to flow into Morocco. As natural gas prices in Europe increase refinery LPG supply will be reduced, the large volume of US imports will continue to maek up for a any supply shortfall.

Spot shipping rates have come off again, reflecting bearish sentiment during the week.   The softening of shipping rates are very much linked to a lack of firm requirement in the market. As vessel availability exceeds the demand, there would be significant discount for prompt ships. With the decline in the spot market, a potential opening arises for charterers to secure term tonnage. Several charterers are actively exploring opportunities for early next year, seeking short-to-medium-term coverage at levels below last done for such period. Thus, taking prompt action to charter for an extended term can prove beneficial at the current levels. Although the market looks quite different this year to last year, there is a cautionary tale in that the majority of vessels are currently under control of subletters, and they can withdraw rapidly if market conditions change. And unfortunately, global events are only adding to these risks and we have seen the LNG price strengthening in recent days.   On the newbuilding front, prices remain firm with reports this week that a far east buyer is linked to an order for one LNG carrier at around US$260M from Samsung Heavy Industries for delivery in September 2026.

Just 5 working days ago, owners were fighting a losing battle to keep WS rates north of the WS 40 level MEG/East. Charterers were eyeing up numbers in the mid WS 30’s and S-Oil (as per usual form) found the bottom of the market at WS 33 (albeit bigger cargo size, better terms, etc). However, it is likely rates fell too quickly, as we write these words, WS 50 reported on subs and owners will be pushing for more as the end October stems are cleared out.   As we have seen many times, the Atlantic market provides the impetus for any improvement. With the WTI vs Dubai price differential closing and thus causing the failing a few vessels USG/East last week, there was a pickup in Brazil and other Atlantic activity. West Africa/East rptd just done at WS 50 and USG/East at USD 7.75m. There is limited tonnage availability for the next 30 days in the Atlantic, so higher numbers likely, certainly with some assistance from the smaller sizes.   A yo-yo market, of which we likely to see more of in the coming months.

The Panamax market witnessed a divergence with significant congestion in Brazil and a tight Pacific market, notably due to Indonesian coal supply disruptions and low minor bulk demand from China. Contrarily, the Atlantic market presented a flat and uneventful week despite occasional spurts of activity in specific routes. The forthcoming market trajectory is closely tied to potential changes in bulk demands and regional coal supply dynamics; we do not expect any significant changes to the Panamax market in the near term.

From the Atlantic, USG become tight on tonnage again. East Mediterranean less volumes, so tonnage might start seeking cargoes from Continent instead. ECSA steady with Ultra fixing about USD 19k from NCSA to East Mediterranean.   Far east holding up, tight on prompt tonnage and rates better there.

The MEG market has benefited from a procession of prompt replacement cargoes that has seen rates reach as high as WS 75/TD23. For the natural window, we freight this run at about WS 65 with no downside. MEG/East will pay circa WS 100 with little to suggest rates will come off this side of the weekend.  The Atlantic market has a generally firm feel with TD20 presently trading just under WS 75 (as of going to print) with rates likely reach WS 80 by the end of the week. A high volume of enquiry against a tight tonnage list will maintain momentum in the region.  The USG Suezmax market is underpinned by a firming Aframax market which will support further upside potential.

We see healthy volume levels on end October to early November C5, East Australia and Pacific. On South Africa and Indian business, we see several enquiries for end October to mid November. On C3 ex Brazil to China, volumes are healthy from operators and 2 major miners for early November and second half of November respectively.  On West Africa, volumes remain comparatively flat. On a whole, market optimism sustained from last week. Tonnage remains tight in Far East and on ballasters. On C5, fixtures concluded at mid USD 10 pmt to low USD 11 pmt levels. On C3, fixtures concluded at a range of mid USD 25 pmt to high USD 26 pmt levels for first half of November stems. One known fixture of a 210k dwt 2024-built scrubber for 2 years at BCI 143% plus sharing basis 75/25% scrubber premium per day.

The market in the North Sea started slower than last week with rates hovering around the WS 100 level for cross North Sea. US markets are stronger providing better returns which has seen tonnage ballast away.  In the short term at least USG looks to remain active which will pull more tonnage away from North Sea reducing the list further. Natural fixing window now pushing into 3rd decade, and we could see rates firming.   Rates steady/firm in the Mediterranean as owners remain bullish in their approach. Has been minimal week on week growth as the market has struggled to navigate outside influences. However, there is a positive feel amongst owners who anticipate incremental rate increases with increased supply, as we progress into winter months. Natural tonnage continues to be picked off though there should be plenty of options looking forward with vessels heading in off the back of TA fixtures and North Sea earnings falling behind slightly making the Mediterranean market a viable option for ballasters.

Headlines at the end of this week are dominated by Frontline & Euronav, and the proposed end to a very public battle for control of the Belgian Tanker giant. John Fredriksen’s Frontline, if approved by regulatory bodies and relevant shareholders, will walk away with 24 Euronav VLCCs in exchange for their 26.12% stake in the company. Transactions this week were concentrated in the MR sector, with five units changing hands. The 22 tanks, fully IMO2 capable TRF BERGEN (49K DWT HYUNDAI VINASHIN 2015) was sold for USD 37M, while EVINOS (49K DWT STX 2013) and SANDPIPER PACIFIC (51K DWT SUNGDONG 2013) both received around USD 34M. Finally, Turkish buyers paying a strong USD 40.5M each for the two 2016 SPP built MR's LACERTA and BORA BORA.   Despite the Golden Week holiday in China, liquidity in the dry sector remains strong. The Capesize market has bounced this week as manufacturing has rebounded. This has filtered down across the dry market where price expectations are firming across the board, meaning those waiting out the bottom of the market might well have missed their chance for now. The standout transaction is Sinokor selling scrubber fitted pair COMANCHE/CHOW (180K DWT SWS 2016) for USD 43.5M each en bloc to buyers Arcelor Mittal, and CONTAMINES (180K DWT SWS 2016) for USD 41.5M to Neda Maritime. Elsewhere, scrubber-fitted Kamsarmax LORD STAR (82K DWT SANOYAS 2013) sold for USD 23.8M.

EAST Looking to the East earnings are now below USD 100k per day for the first time since the end of August. The East/West earnings spread has come in a bit since yesterday, but it may look like East currently has more downside than what we find currently in the West. We are now counting a total of 21 spot fixtures ex Middle East for October (average so far this year stands at 23) and with tonnage availability still plentiful with about a dozen potential open vessels still on end Oct dates it should be fair to suggest we might see freight coming off further before an eventual floor is found.  WEST The West market has been more or less muted for the last two weeks as a change in sentiment has been looming and also in the wake of Asian holidays taking place this week. In the short term, the drop in freight rates of about USD 50 per ton seems to have taken the edge off the waiting game, however, it remains to be seen if the last done fixture at USD 200 Houston/Chiba off end November ex USG is the bottom or not. Although the drop in rates on a per-ton basis may feel and seem brutal, the market is still trading above USD 100k per day! Up till today, we've seen about 10 spot fixtures ex USG/EC for November, which compared with an average of about 30 fixtures per month implies that we will see more deals concluded in the weeks to come.

comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: NWE An end October TOT window bid at CIF ARA October flat saw an early November TOT offer surface at November CIF ARA minus $2/MT.  Term imports to the region continue to satisfy demand as petrochemical demand remains low whilst unseasonably warm temperatures are keeping incremental winter demand at bay. Butane values dropped significantly, now valued at 78.5% October Naphtha from 82%, while the main loss in value came from naphtha values dropping $20/MT since Wednesday. Linked to the large drop in crude oil values this week Brent coming off from $91/bbl Tuesday to $84/bbl Thursday.     MED Large trans-Atlantic volumes continue to be imported to the region. While the hottest September on record is keeping demand subdued. Leading to a quiet week in the spot market.  AMERICAS  Mont Belvieu propane levels have so far not succumbed to the weight of domestic inventory levels, but instead have been more swayed by crude, which until late September was on a slow but steady upward march that concluded in the low $90’s/bbl range – which propane values followed.  As of the start of October, though, there have only been declines in the crude arena and, as such, the trajectory of propane has mostly mirrored WTI, remaining all the while at a ratio in the 33-34% range.   As for the inventories themselves, most of the market this week was anticipating a correction last week’s data, which revealed a reported build that was well below expectations.  This week the EIA data confounded even more, as a 0.00mmbbl build (or draw) was reported, leaving overall stocks at 101.4mmbbls when an average of +1.75mmbbls was predicted (and historically has seen a 2.4mmbbl rise).  Whether or not this marks the conclusion of the traditional build season – or whether a large correction is now in order - remains to be seen, but up until now an overall total had been pegged at the 105mmbbl level as of end-Sep.   As for the terminal fee market, things had been cooling off and a Nov transaction was reported in the low 10cpg range with buyers retreating to single digits.  More recently, though, there was an about-face and an end-Oct was this week rumored at 13cpg.  Offers are now in the low teens range, with buy-side interest seemingly skeptical but nonetheless rising, as well

comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: No report due to Golden Week public holiday

We typically expect a strengthened freight market in LNG as we head into the Northern Hemisphere’s winter months. However, this week has shown no signs of that, as headline rates are lower and ballast bonuses remain unchanged at round trip. The prospects of any profitable contango play appear bleak now, yet gas markets refuse to provide participants with any sustained direction to date. European inventory levels are currently high, and TTF has fallen this week which may in turn further solidify decisions to redirect laden vessels towards the East. In the Atlantic, requirements that were previously lingering have been fixed at lower levels compared to previous deals. In the Pacific, many major players have been inactive due to holidays in China and Korea, coupled with high inventory levels in Japan. However, as the week progresses and requirements start to firm up, we anticipate increased activity in this region, which may stem the decline. While the signs point to a weaker freight market, it's noteworthy that Charterers are attempting to extend the fixing window into December. There haven't been any new build orders placed in the past week, however, QatarEnergy has taken steps to reserve 17 slots at HHI.

Signs of life in the Atlantic where TD20 has slowly traded up to about WS 70 with the fixing window focused on the third decade (October).  On a positive note, there is support from across the Atlantic where a steady stream of USG lightering opportunities have trimmed the early side of the list, but worth noting that this region is fed on a diet of mainly local ships with the respective fixing windows (W.Africa/USG) out of kilter with each other dates wise. On a slightly more negative tone, the Mediterranean is still well stocked with tonnage due to constant replenishment from TD 23 voyages, so if there is further upside in West Africa, it's likely to be modest.  In the East, steady enquiry levels should see TD 23 trade out the balance of the week at WS 60, whilst a MEG/China run should remain steady at circa WS 97.5-100 NHC.

The week started and remained at healthy volume levels on mid-late October C5, East Australia and Pacific. On South Africa and Indian business, we see a slight uptick from last week. On C3 ex Brazil to China, we see healthy volumes from operators and a major miner. On West Africa, volumes remain relatively flat. On a whole, there has been an uptick in market optimism and activity. Far East and ballasting tonnage is tight. On C5, fixtures concluded higher than last week at low-mid USD 10 pmt levels. On C3, fixtures concluded at mid USD 24 pmt levels for late October stems. On period, we continue to see limited activity with one known fixture of a 208k dwt, 2020-build, non-scrubber for 9 to 11 months at USD 24,000 per day.

The Supramax FFA market has been up all week long despite the holiday season in China. However, the physical market remains at a low with barely any activity on the spot market. Traders in China had covered their positions well before the mid-autumn festival. There has been a dip in the PG-WCI rates for Supra/Ultras and heard couple’ vessels open spot and awaiting next employment. Meantime, effective November 01st, 2023 and until further notice, Panamax Plus transits are suspended. Panamax size vessels must transit the Panamax Locks complying with the corresponding maximum TFW draft for the Old Locks. We can expect to see a potential ripple effect of this new regulation on geared vessel sizes in the coming months. Hope we can see activity pick up next week once the traders are back in office in China.

Not the rosiest of weeks gone by for the VLCC market that’s for sure. Last week closed out with tonnage building in the East and putting pressure on the WS 50 mark for TD3 runs, and sure enough the inevitable happened this week with charterers managing to score in the low WS 40s. The outlook for the back end of this week in the MEG is not looking great. It's now down to the owning community to draw a line in the sand, but this will come at a cost.   In the West, there is still a good cohort of ships ballasting to the Cape and a decent enough supply of local list of ships to pick up any volume that comes from that side of the globe. The story of the week has been Brazil/East fixing twice and the most recent being WS 44.75 for a China run. USG/East sits somewhere in the upper 7m’s about now with some downward bias given how little volume we have seen.

The Panamax market is experiencing a cautious period, with lingering high congestion in Brazil and a spread-out fleet, especially noticeable to the west of Suez. Despite Asia's high demand for coal, vessel counts to key Pacific regions are notably low. Market activity is overall slow and bearish, particularly in the Atlantic and Asian sectors, partly due to holiday impacts. Meanwhile, the Pacific market is subtly softening, with participants holding a wait-and-see attitude amidst the mixed signals in various locales.

The North Sea Aframax market started the week with an influx of activity which saw rates push up from last done, but on the surface has now gone a bit quieter.  Natural window now 11-13 October.  Ballasting USG remains an attractive option for certain tonnage which will keep a check on the list even with vessels coming into the area. Activity has shown consistent flow the past week helping to maintain steady levels in the Mediterranean. Natural tonnage still looks relatively tight for current fixing window as dates push forward and with continued supply, we expect to see owners hold firm. Recent USG action has given owners an outlet for vessels sat off Europe wanting a home and with opportunities in other markets there to entertain, would expect rates to remain steady-ish with any movement wanting to be in an upward trend. Suezmaxes will be watching with interest... again.

The standout transaction in the Tanker market is CRUDESUN/CRUDEMED (115K DWT DAEHAN 2018) sold for USD 70M each. We understand the vessels are fixed to Unipec for 3 years at USD 40K/day. A further transaction in the Aframax/LR2 sector is PS VENEZIA (108K DWT HUDONG ZHONGHUA 2010) at USD 37.5M (DD Due) to Vietnamese buyers Fgas, notably fetching a lower-than-expected price in what is quite an in-demand part of the Afra/LR2 age curve, even with surveys due. Elsewhere SHANDONG ZIHE (40K DWT SHINA 2004) sold via online bidding platform at USD 14.45M.  Volume in the dry sector remains high, with sales across the size curve this week. This comes despite murmurs in the market of a possible slight further softening in the space before the anticipated recovery, only time will tell when we hit the bottom of this dry cycle. JP Morgan acquired 3x large handysize vessels FENGNING/FUNING/FOOCHOW (39K DWT CHENGXI 2015) for USD 19.5M each, around the same levels as last done on a 2015 unit (CIELO DI VALPARAISO) at USD 20M in March 2023. Offers were due this week on Capesize SUIGO (174K DWT NAMURA 2011), and she was eventually sold at USD 23.5M to Greek buyers.

comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG Saudi Aramco set Oct CP at $600 for C3 and $615 for C4, up by $50 and $55 respectively. This is higher than curve value and players’ expectations. This being said, the strong crude, robust demand against tight supply on AG FOBs, together with the high FEI/CP spread all lend supports to the CP. Additionally, premium for evenly split cargos for Oct liftings was assessed earlier at Oct CP plus 40s, especially with Indian majors emerged for spot inquiries continuously. At the time of writing, Nov CP was traded at $606.   FAR EAST Cash premium inched up this week on 23/0 for both 2h Oct and 1h Nov delivery in window. Such parcel was bid at Oct FEI plus $5 for 2h Oct, and Nov FEI plus $2 for 1h Nov. Outside window some 46/0 parcels for 1h Nov delivery were changed hand at price reported at Nov FEI plus high single digit basis NChina.   Buying inquires for feedstock are active this week. FPC awarded their buy tender for mid Nov delivery full propane cargo at Nov FEI plus mid-single digit into Ningbo, and their 600kt/y PDH unit is expected to do trial run soonest. One Vietnam based PDH user reported to buy Nov delivery propane at Nov CP plus $100s, while the other SChina PDH user cancelled similar tender due to high offers. One NChina PDH managed to secure a Nov delivered full propane cargo at Nov FEI plus high single digit reportedly. Another EChina cracker also reported have bought 23kt propane for 1st decade Nov arrival into Ningbo.   Apart from propane, Indian IOC retendered to procure in total 4 evenly split cargos for Nov and Dec delivery, after they failed to award their last one.

EAST Freight assessments, especially in the East where the end of October position list is getting a bit longer every day, are coming down sharply. One India cargo that some were expecting to come out for end of the month dates now seems to be covered internally and it would be optimistic to expect anything more than 4-5 cargoes to be uncovered for the remaining of October. As such the market is looking long and sentiment has in short time gone from super bull to rather bearish. This should naturally draw the fixing window closer, which coupled with the upcoming Autumn Festival in China, could mean we won’t see much spot action for the next 7-10 days or so unless some owners are willing to do significantly lower levels than of last done.  WEST So far this week we have only seen two spot fixtures in the West and they were both relets concluded at 250 H/C and 150 H/F. With the western position list growing lately and the arb weakening a bit we have now seen the willingness to fix a vessel slow down. Current fixing window is 6-7 weeks ahead and charterers seem comfortable waiting while seeing freight rates decrease.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: AMERICAS  The EIA this week posted an inventory gain of 700,000bbls when the market was anticipating something on the order of +2mmbbls (the 5-year average weekly build is 650,000bbls).  However, exports this month have been impacted by a recent electrical outage which caused compressor failure at one terminal, and mandatory government inspections at another, leaving many with the impression that overall export volumes should have theoretically declined and thus allowing domestic stock levels to grow at a greater rate.  But the EIA data shows that export volumes over the 38th week were as high as 2+mmbbls/day, which is well contrary to what had been anticipated.   Overall propane inventories as of the week ending 22 Sep stand at 101.4mmbbls, or 122% of last year, and 139% of 2021.  The market still generally expects that the high point will likely be around 105mmbbls in the coming weeks when the traditional ‘build’ season concludes and winter-related demand commences.   The price at Mont Belvieu should likely have been negatively impacted by the lofty inventory levels, but crude has taken control and as it is now in the $92-93/bbl range so propane prices at MB have seen recent price gains to the ~74cts/gal level.   Meanwhile, based on a rapidly declining arb, terminal fees are in retreat from the high point of 15+ cts/gal (for Nov) and cargoes – few that they are – are being offered at just above a dime (10cts/gal) but buyers have the upper single-digits in mind – if a vessel is available.  NWE Europe continues to manage to temp US volumes as constraints to taking a cargoes East, such as Panama Canal delays and tight freight keep Europe relevant. The October East/West spread around $120/MT not including the physical discount in the window, October CIF ARA minus $8/MT while the Ginga window is at November FEI +2/MT. The price difference has not stopped Europe importing 500,000MT in September and October likely to exceed this, with 260,000MT set to arrive in the first half of the month. Butane is at 82% October Naphtha, a large rise in outright value, as crude oil and naphtha saw large gains. In line with the strong level set for October CP and for the expected seasonal rise in demand.   MED Butane in the West Med moved up into the 96% spot Naphtha, on the back of strong bidding for a Lavera FOB.  Much more typical ratio for the time of year. US Butane continues to be imported into Morocco. CP being set at $600/MT propane and $615/MT butane will continue to see split ratio US cargoes head for the East Med market.

Negative sentiment is present across both basins. In Asian markets in view of the upcoming Golden Week, the demand for prompt tonnage in Asia decreased level flattened out. After a period of strong positive sentiment in the Atlantic, rates started to soften, and premiums for the larger Ultramax units were said to have seen significant drops. In the US Gulf, cargo availability for transatlantic and front haul were both said to have declined leading to charterers reducing ideas.   In the Atlantic, Supramaxes is fixing levels of around USD 25,000 for FH from the Continent and Mediterranean to the Far East. From USG we see a wide range and significant gap between bids and offers that vary anything from low USD 20,000 to high USD 20,000. In ECSA, Ultra is rumored fixed USD 16,000 plus USD 600,000 GBB with grain cargo to Singapore-Japan. We expect the market to be quieter next week with sideways development.

It is far from a full swing in sentiment this week for the VLCCs, but perhaps a halt in further upticks, as the market appears to have taken a breather. Not to say that alarm bells are ringing in owner’s offices, but at or around last done levels now seems more probable than any further upward trajectory short term in the MEG. Owners holding the line north of WS 50 for regular TD3C, but for every quiet day (at least on the surface), a little more could be chipped off.   The Atlantic is looking a bit more wanting however.  The WTI-Dubai discount is under pressure with a backwardated forward curve. More than a couple of USG load fixtures failed yesterday and there are 9 committed ballasters to the Cape of Good Hope, all from different owners. The hope is for West Africa and Brazil to pick up the slack.

The East Suezmax market has been highly volatile with MEG/China rates now hovering around the WS 100 mark. TD23 has thus far been insulated from these movements as owners look to reposition West with this run pricing about WS 55-60.  There's a flat feel in the Atlantic basin with TD20 stable at WS 67.5 and USG/TA repeating WS 45.   Bad weather and shorter nights are yet to impact the Black Sea with TD6 charterers benefiting from of an armada of ships opening up in the Mediterranean (off the back of TD23 voyages). This will keep TD6 pinned down at WS 72.5 for the balance of the week.

The week started with a moderate level for early-mid October C5 cargo. Volumes remain healthy on East Australia and Pacific. Moving into mid-week, South Africa and India volumes are flat. On C3 ex Brazil to China, volume is healthy. Volumes for West Africa has improved from previous weeks as we see several fresh enquiries for late October-early November stems. Far East tonnage remain tight. Number of ballasters dwindled further from last week. On C5, fixtures concluded higher at high USD 9 pmt to low USD 10 pmt levels. On C3, we see fixtures concluding at mid to high USD 23 pmt levels for 15th October onwards. On period, we continue to see limited activity with one fixture detailing a 179k dwt 2011-build non-scrubber for 21 to 24 months at USD 17,500 per day.

It has been a rather surprising week on LNG pricing since we have seen the paper market forfeit most of the contango opportunities until December, which is likely driven by high gas inventories and an early forecast of milder than average temperatures for the start of the winter in Europe. This has created some uncertainty with regards to what might happen to the LNG shipping rates, since LNG prices are still high enough to avoid any cargo cancellations keeping supply intact, but on the other hand, we might see fewer floating opportunities and more available tonnage, unless of course we start seeing congestion at various disports. Throw into the mix the constantly fluctuating arbitrage and we a have proper conundrum on our hands! On the prompt however, we are seeing a bit of softening on the spot rates in both basins, and with only limited prompt opportunities to be worked, some vessels might see some idling ahead. We are seeing some charter opportunities for November and even for December, but these laycans are still a bit far out, and proposed levels are staying relatively strong amidst this uncertainty. On the newbuilding market, we have not recorded any new orders in the past week, but yards are keeping busy finalising the paintjobs in order to deliver a legion of shiny newbuilds for Q4 2023 and Q1 2024.

The Panamax market remains robust with firming rates in the Atlantic despite recent highs and a mild increase in South ex East Coast South America rates. Asia maintains a neutral stance with older vessels seeing more traction, especially ex Indonesia. While the Atlantic experiences a surge in grains and minerals activity, the Pacific market shows signs of deceleration. Market indicators hinted at potential weakening, yet the coal and iron ore sectors are seeing increased activity. With the upcoming mid-Autumn festival holidays in Asia and the long holiday in China, an active week is expected, albeit with caution in interpreting market trends.

It has been yet another quiet week for Aframax Owners trading in the North Sea. Lack of activity still keep rates at bottom levels. Some Owners have ballasted away from the area to seek better opportunities elsewhere. We can only expect a recovery in rates once activity picks up.The past week proved to be a bit more interesting in the Mediterranean, and rates ticked up on the back of increased activity. However, sentiment is now changing and there is a softer feeling to the market. Although, the cap on the Med Aframax market from the Suezmaxes has become so ever apparent, the natural Aframax tonnage is still relatively tight in the region. The backlog of traffic in Trieste and the consistency of volume will be two key factors in keeping the pressure on current levels. The limits been put on rates in this region have caused concerns for Owners, but we cannot see rates falling significantly much below where we are now going forward.

A relatively quiet week in the second-hand tanker market with much of the industry’s attention focused on the newbuilding story. 11% of the existing Suezmax fleet is now on order, this subsector seeing the highest number of orders in a single year in the past decade. Behind the scenes however, Aframax tanker interest is swelling, and owners are seemingly happy to part with tonnage, often at hugely attractive levels to what they initially purchased their ships for. Particularly FULMAR (115K DWT 2009 HANJIN HI), sold to Middle Eastern buyers at USD 39.5M, almost double what Union Maritime paid for the unit in 2019 at auction. Older large tankers seem to have cooled with the sale of VLCC GOOD NEWS (319K DWT 2002 HHI) at just under USD 35M, a unit that was asking over USD 40M before the summer. Pyxis has sold its eco MR tanker PYXIS EPSILON (50K DWT 2015 SPP) for a whopping USD 40.7M to US buyers. At this stage we can only speculate if the deal is linked to the US Tanker Security Program aimed at boosting access to commercial product tankers to safeguard oil shipping for its armed forces.   Liquidity in the Dry sector continues to grow as it feels ‘now is the time’ to make a move. All sizes of modern Japanese built tonnage appear on most prospective buyers’ wish lists, thus making available units highly competitive. Those willing to look at slightly older units are seeing an increased availability of candidates, something which will excite potential asset players. In the Kamsarmax sector, WESTERN MONACO (81K DWT 2016 HANTONG) was sold for a firm USD 26M while NORD SUN (82K DWT 2013 TSUNEISHI CEBU) was bought by Greek buyers at USD 21.8M. Elsewhere, Capesize GRACIOUS ETERNITY (180K DWT 2009 IMABARI) was sold to Chinese buyers at USD 21.9M.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: AMERICAS Mont Belvieu propane market levels are in retreat after the EIA inventory data for the week ending 15 Sep showed a 1.6mmbbl build which pushed overall stocks to 100.7mmbbls – which was entirely expected, but nonetheless is an important milestone, if only from a psychological perspective.   In any case, there are a couple of weeks remaining in the traditional propane inventory build season and it is pretty widely anticipated because of the high production levels and simultaneously reduced export levels that stocks will in the next couple of weeks broach the 105mmbbl level.  As such, the pricing structure – which has lately been aligned with the strength of the crude markets – has reversed course and is now back in the low/mid 71cts/gal range.   Terminal fees, meanwhile, appear to have crested (at least for the moment) as offers for 1H Nov are presently seen in the 11-12cpg range and buy-side interest exists in the 9-10cpg range.  Shipping remains the stumbling point, however, as delays (and therefore costs) associated with the Panama Canal have forced a number of shipowners to transit via the Cape of Good Hope and/or Suez Canal.  Those routes require additional sailing days which, thus, further exacerbates shipping avails.  NWE The TOT window has been quiet since a 9-13 October offer pushed assessed physical values to -$11/MT to October CIF ARA. US tons continue to head to the region even though petrochemical demand remains low, tipping the market to long. The October East/West spread $116/MT will continue to see US spot cargoes head East. Many spot VLGC fixtures not offering West options to lock in sky high freight rates on longer voyages. Which could make it difficult for European buyers to attract cargoes to the region if demand rises. Butane remains at 88% September Naphtha, though trading has been quiet as crude oil & naphtha price swings have made it difficult to pin down a northwest European butane value.   MED The region continues to import large volumes of LPG, with 110,000MT set to arrive in the region in early October. Turkish demand has stayed strong and mixed ratio VLGC demand continues.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG Saudi released their acceptance with no cuts but also no plus tolerance for term liftings. KPC sold a 12/13 Oct lifting full propane via tender. Evenly split cargos are still in tight supply and was bid at the equivalence of CP plus mid 30s in the window. At the time of writing, Oct C3 CP was traded at $569 and C4 at $10 higher.   FAR EAST Cash premium for 23kt propane parcels for Oct delivery inched up this week as less offers available, together with the US loading delays and the soaring freight. Such parcel was traded in window during mid-week at Oct FEI plus $0.5. 46kt propane for 1h Nov delivery was reported concluded at Nov FEI plus low single digit basis NChina.   Off window a flurry of tenders ongoing for both propane and butane. Last Friday FPC awarded their buy tender for an evenly split cargo delivered in 2h Oct at Oct MOPJ minus high teens. And Pertamina tendered to buy two cargos of such grade for Nov delivery, while IOC also reported to procure same for both Nov and Dec delivery. Other than butane, three PDH users issued tender to secure both Oct and Nov delivered propane as feedstock. Apart from spot, one Chinese Major also issued term tender to procure monthly 46/0 for 2024 delivery and we believe more importers will start to renew their negotiate on new terms soon.

EAST After a small handful of late Indian cargo quotes hitting a very tight shipping market Owners have basically named their price and last done India deal now at above 200 RT/C equivalent and latest non-Indian done at low 180s RT/C. The regular fixing window in the East is now well into last decade of October  where sentiment from both a strong US market and the record levels concluded for India deals have spilled over to the Ras Tanura - Chiba route. This means we are fixing more than a month ahead where itineraries are somewhat blurry for most vessels and the asking price and last done is reflecting same.  WEST Starting off the week we found the BLPG3 index at low 220s H/C and in just a few days we have seen it jump to about 250 H/C - this rate gives a daily TCE of approximately 150k. Although seeing these high rates the West is still trading at a discount of about 30 pmt compared to the East. At the time of writing we count 6 spot fixtures out of the USG/USEC for November dates and the position list for 1H Nov is already looking extremely slim showing only a few workable positions left for the uncovered cargoes out there. With that said there should be more room for western freight rates to continue increasing.

A week for the owning community to savor. With a tightening position list and charterers looking to cover the start of their October program, MEG rates have ticked up. A solid WS 41 paid to Taiwan early this week shows modern tonnage can push when needed. Next done, pick a number in the WS 40’s. Older/disadvantaged tonnage may offer an escape valve, but they are increasingly in short supply, as we have seen ex dd’s quickly picked off by those who can. TD3C paper has jumped +10 point for the next few months which will also help sentiment, even if it is people look to go long where they can.   As for the Atlantic, close to USD 8m paid off end October dates USG/China, following on from an early October replacement deal at similar levels. This highlights the tightness of the list for any October dates in the USG, with many vessels that are there wishing to stay West, not willing to see out Q4 at current levels. Many ships on uncertain itineraries too, reluctant to commit in danger of running late. USD 6.4m paid for USG/WC India twice, a little old and a perfect run for a Bahri relet. With West Africa/East now at WS 49.5, owners will not have to work hard to build on that.

Congestion in South America is the highest since early last year, and in Indonesia it is close to all-time highs. Year-to-date highs made in vessels in or heading to the North Atlantic/Europe Continent, and vessels in or heading to the South Atlantic remain close to year-to-date highs.  Overall, the market is looking strong. The usual seasonal pattern has not been followed this year, but “on average” the market continues to climb until late October before trending down into year-end.

While rates remained relatively stable last week, the dynamics have shifted significantly this week due to a surge in vessel requirements in both basins. Although there are vessels available, Charterers are showing a clear preference for larger vessels to lift the larger cargo parcels especially in the West, leading to a perceived scarcity of LNG vessels available for charter. In the East, there has still been a market for the smaller steam turbine vessels. As a result, charter rates have increased from last week's levels, and this upward trend is expected to continue throughout the week, as vessel requirements remain unfulfilled as of today. Floating storage taking advantage of the contango situation are still occupying shipping capacities.   There have been no reports of newbuilding orders this week, as ship prices show no signs of weakening and demand for shipbuilding slots continues to be robust.

NORTH It has been quite a sluggish week for Aframax owners trading in the North Sea. Lack of activity has kept rates at bottom levels and the tonnage list is building up. However, some owners might turn their bow towards the Mediterranean as that market looks a bit more interesting. A positive recovery can only be expected once we move into October fixing dates.   MEDITERRANEAN Tables turned quickly in the Mediterranean earlier this week as charterers kept coming out with end-September inquiries and position list suddenly got tighter. Sentiment is changing and owners are in the mood to push for more and more now. October dates have started kicking in and if activity remains healthy, we will probably see further improvement on the rates.

The week started with healthy volumes for late September-early October C5, East Australia and Pacific business, contributing to a further increase in optimism. Volumes on C5 tapered off mid-week while East Australia remains high. Early October South Africa and India volumes hold at reasonable levels. On C3 ex Brazil to China, the week started off quiet, but activity level started picked up mid-week for mid-October stems. For West Africa, we see fresh enquiries, but volume remains comparatively lower than other trades. Far East and ballasting tonnage further tightened this week. C5 levels increased substantially from last week, with fixtures concluding at mid USD 9 pmt levels. On C3, discussions are at USD 21 pmt level for end September to early October stems. Fixtures concluded at mid USD 22 pmt for 15th October onwards. On period, we continue to see limited activity with one known fixture of a 171k dwt 2005-build non-scrubber for spread of 4 to 6 months at USD 14,000 per day.

The global Suezmax market is showing latent signs of potential with West Africa and MEG arguably the most interesting load zones. The MEG list is very tight for 20 ton crane availability (first decade October), which has underpinned rates this week. As we go to print, WS 100 is on subs for a Fujairah/East voyage (1-10/10 window), with no apparent downside, despite the background threat of cannibalization from VLCCs.  In the Atlantic, there is a perception, although possibly misplaced, that a weak USG market will start to weigh down TD20. We're not completely comfortable with this perception as the make-up of the list (7-12 October) in West Africa is not that straightforward and even more pertinent, prompt USG ships are unlikely to ballast across the pond as an active USG VLCC market bodes positively for the weeks ahead.

The Panamax market is holding strong, driven largely by congestion in Brazil and a solid performance in the Asia sector. Despite stagnant demand in the North Atlantic and mixed results in other areas, firm sentiment and a strong FFA market continue to nudge rates upward. The current outlook remains cautiously optimistic, anchored by sustained activity in the Atlantic and steady demands in late September and early October.

No action on the larger Tanker front this week as spot rates continue to give a lethargic feel to what is fundamentally, a strong market. Interest, however, seems to be swirling around the Aframax space with a number of candidates entering the market. CENTENNIAL SAPPORO (110K DWT Mitsui 2008) bought by Beks for USD 35.5M with delivery SS due, and FULMAR (115K DWT Hanjin HI 2009) at USD 39.5M to Middle Eastern buyers will certainly help guide the growing list of enquiries. In the MR space, SUNNY APATITE (49K DWT GSI 2016) sold for USD 34M, while GRAND ACE8 (46K DWT HMD 2008) at USD 23.8M with SS passed, showing that despite a cooling since highs of earlier this year there remains robust interest in this sector.  Activity across Dry remains strong as prices stabilise. The most notable of the recent deals is 4 x Crown 63 Dayang Ultramax units GIANTS CAUSEWAY/SADLERS WELLS/GALILEO/CAPE CROSS (63K DWT 2014-2015) being bought en bloc at USD 86M by Greek buyers. This provides an interesting benchmark for what is clearly a high level of buying interest of modern Ultramaxes. Two transactions in the Kamsarmax sector as GENEVA STAR (81K DWT Tsuneishi Cebu 2015) received numerous offers, eventually going to Chinese buyers at USD 26.5M, and CUMA (83K DWT Tsuneishi 2006) acquired by Bulkseas for USD 13.2M.

EAST The list of available positions for first half of October in the AG is getting slimmer now as a small handful of ships have been taken out both in the East and in the West. There are still some cargos in the works in this period, and more cargos are expected to hit the market later on as well for 1H October dates. So far this week freight remains stable in both regions and with the current activity level the threat of any imminent drop in freight seams bleak.     WEST Although we have seen as much as 38 spot fixtures in October ex USG/USEC only 13 of them have been done in 2H Oct. Compared to the YTD average for 2H of a month we find October three spot fixtures behind. We have already seen the first fixture in November, but October fixing does not seem completely finished just yet as there are still a couple open positions left in October and a few Charterers still out looking. The Western market is currently trading at a discount of about 15 dollars to the East before waiting in the Panama Canal as we see last done fixture ex USG at mid-low 220s H/C and mid-low 120 H/F.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG AG supply still appears tight with Indian PSUs asking for optional cargos. Evenly split cargo was bid at Oct lifting at CP plus $25 but no offers seen in window. At the time of writing, Oct C3 CP was traded at $570 and C4 at $5 higher. Oct/Nov C3 widened further to $16.   FAR EAST Cash premium for 23kt propane parcels softened for Oct delivery. Earlier such parcel for 2h Oct delivery was changed hand at Oct FEI plus $5, however offered down to flattish level on Thurs. Similar parcel for 1h Nov delivery was offered at Nov FEI minus $4. The Oct FEI/CP enlarged to $120, highest surpassed $130, partly owing to the freight, has refrained the buying interest.   Off window a handful of tenders floating. One EChina PDH user secured 23kt propane parcel at Oct FEI plus low teens reportedly. One Korean player also tendered to buy 23kt butane for 2h Oct delivery for cracking. One heavy propane cargo of Australia origin for 2h Oct delivery was reported sold into Japan at FEI plus mid-high teens. Another oil major also tendered to procure evenly split cargo for Oct lifting or Oct delivery into Port Klang. FPC also tenders to buy Oct delivery LPG at flexible ratio, max 23kt for each grade.   China PDHs are still reluctant to move as negative margins on soaring feedstock price, with some adjusting rates or plan to advance scheduled maintenance. Despite such, several new PDHs are still expected to start up in Q4 with indispensable feedstock demand.

The Aframax market in the North Sea hit bottom level end of last week with rates hovering around WS 92.5-95 level. The soft sentiment continued into this week. Despite a tighter tonnage list, we still need to see a bigger cargo volume before we will see any improvement in rates. More of the same in the BSea/Med with rates taking another hit and reaching new low levels. Activity was moderate last week as well and despite charterers fixing for forward dates the rates remained poor. We don’t expect any upside potential in the short term as tonnage list is still long enough and surrounding areas don’t offer better alternatives.

Overall sentiment remained very positive in both the Atlantic and Asia basins. Most loading areas seeing rates increasing and owners demanding more money for forward positions.    Activity is picking up on the East of Suez and we’re finally seeing lots of cargo orders coming in this morning, especially MEG-India region. 56k dwt heard fixed for EC India to China went for USD 8k, however we expect markets to move up this week.   The FFA opened with a bang and up by USD 300+ and we can see a busy season ahead in the coming months.

Following the resounding success of the Gastech conference in Singapore, LNG shipping is riding a wave of renewed optimism. Industry players have returned to their offices around the world with fresh insights and a collaborative spirit, and are now directing their attention towards chartering in preparation for the impending winter season and supporting ADP processes for next year. We are at the time of year when floating cargoes may start to emerge, and there is a contango through to December and with storage levels high there is also operational storage on the table. Risks to the downside include geopolitical factors (or industrial strikes) that could disrupt supply chains and influence pricing, although as we saw last year in particular such factors can reduce volume but higher LNG prices can produce a frenzy to secure tonnage. As the LNG shipping landscape evolves, stakeholders are closely monitoring these dynamics to make informed decisions and seize opportunities in this dynamic sector.  This week saw no newbuilding orders, with the persistently limited availability of shipyard slots and the ongoing strength in newbuilding prices.

The Panamax market remains buoyant, with high vessel counts in East Coast South America boosting a rally that has seen the BPI index reach new highs since July, with a 10.2% increase week-to-week. Factors such as increased vessels heading to the US and a low vessel presence East of Suez could further spur the rally. Despite a slow start this week, strong demand from the US Gulf and NC South America has driven up rates, with a notable increase in front haul trips. The market is watchful, optimistic about sustained growth with potential lifts envisaged in October.

VLCCs are coming more into play and diluting/capping Suezmax rates. A case in point is a Basrah/West-East stem that is presently looking at both vessel classes. TD23 has traded mid/high WS 50's this week and has only been saved by the fact that Suezmax tend to work out marginally cheaper when going through the ditch (plus port restrictions on larger ladies). However, if the cargo needs to go East, it's a no brainer to take a VLCC over a Suezmax.  The wider Atlantic has a flat fleet with no evident upswing in the offing. TD23 will trade out the balance of the week in the low WS 70's with TD6 pinned down at a steady WS 72.5.

The week started with significant volumes for mid-late September C5, East Australia, and Pacific business, contributing to an uptick in optimism. Late September, South Africa and India volumes hold at reasonably healthy levels. On C3 ex Brazil to China, the week started off quiet and we see very scarce late September-early October stems. C3 activity level increased slightly mid-week for mid Oct. Tonnage in Far East is dwindling but number of ballasters remain substantial. C5 levels increased slightly from last week, with fixtures concluding at low-mid USD 8 pmt levels. On C3, owners are adopting a conservative approach. Limited fixtures concluding at USD 20 pmt level. On period, we see very limited activity with only one known fixture detailing a 180k DWT 2013 build non-scrubber for one year.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: AMERICAS In a rather classic case of the market becoming “overdone”, spot terminal fees for 1H October rocketed upwards in late August and early September, reaching heights not seen for some years as a couple of transactions were noted above 15cpg.  Asking levels went even higher but the headwinds that accumulated alongside such levels became too great – particularly in the face of rising freight costs and delays associated with the lack of rain at the Panama Canal.  As such terminal fees for 2H have declined into what is now deemed to be the low ‘teens’ range.  The timing of shipping (and availability), though, remains a concern.  Meanwhile, 1H Nov is presently offered at 11cpg and bid in the 10s – still rather high from a historical perspective, but generally supported by the Eastern arb.   All the while the EIA reported on Wed that propane stock levels as of 08 Sep increased by 3.1mmbbls to 99.1mmbbls – well above the 5-year high point of 97.380mmbbls, 127% of last year, and 140% of two years ago.  There exists at this point no reason to believe that overall US propane inventory levels won’t reach 105mmbbls by the end of the month, and well positioning the market for what is increasingly expected to be a colder-than-average winter.   Otherwise, the persistent high heat in the US South and Midwest regions may have finally begun to abate, but nonetheless the production and transportation systems across the nation continue to struggle, perhaps most notably a recent power outage which caused several days lifting delays at one of the terminals.  Current estimates are calling for a full roster within the month of September, though.  NWE A TOT window deal was done between BP and ENI as BP raised their 3-8 October buying idea to a fixed price of $588/MT where it was booked. 26-30 September TOT cargo continued to be offered by ENI which pushed end September physical premium down $0.50/MT to September CIF ARA +$4/MT. September Northwest European import volumes look set to be above 450,000MT. It is not yet know if petchem demand will rise in October as some plants are set to go on maintenance while others come back online. Butane demand is starting to see the seasonal demand increase and although values are stable at 83.5% Naphtha outright value has increased with rising naphtha and crude oil.   MED The full effects of the devastating earthquake in Morocco and floods in Libya are not yet known. Mediterranean imports have been steady at a large volume of over 400,000MT for the past 11months. Flat price gains continue in the region due to rising crude.

Plenty of deals continue under the radar as rates continue to struggle gaining traction. The September MEG stems are almost at a completion, bar a few very end month stems and/or replacement deals. A healthy volume, with close to 150 cargoes lifted, is a clear USD 30+ million barrels more than the August total. Despite this, tonnage remains in abundance with plenty of ships hanging over into October and rates continue to hover around the WS 36-37 level for TD3C.   In the Atlantic, there is a little more expectation for upward movement, but not by any big jumps, as tonnage remains a little tighter for prompter dates. Any owners looking at a ballast via cape, given the current low rates, locking in a long ballast and it closing out your year, all makes it a little less attractive. As such, fewer ships may be willing to make the move until we see a little improvement.   Although the market and present rates seem in the doldrums, September is consistently the month with weakest rates and those with a good memory will know these markets can change quick. With oil price knocking on USD 95, OPEC may need to rethink production cuts in due course.

ATHENIAN FREEDOM (299K DWT 2013 HHI) to Chinese buyers (scrubber to be installed prior delivery) at USD 78M, and Tsakos fixing a VLCC on 3yr charter for USD 55k/day signals the underlying strength of the tanker story, despite the limp spot market and talk of lagging Chinese demand. Older large tankers still hold their value, with Chinese buyers paying USD 37.8M for LILA ORLANDO (158K DWT 2005 DSME). Elsewhere, Bahri offloaded 2x Zinc-coated MRs in the form of NCC NAJD/HIJAZ (45K DWT 2005 HMD) at USD 17.2M each.    Across the bulk market, buyers are jostling for tonnage as some market participants speculate that we have either reached, or are about to reach, the bottom of the market. There will be a healthy flow of sales from now until the end of the year, not because owners are suffering, but because they will want to position themselves and structure their fleets to profit from improving conditions next year. Ultramax SANTA MARIA (61K DWT 2014 IMABARI) sold to Greek buyers at USD 23.5M, reinforcing the ongoing value correction. Enquiry has picked up dramatically in recent weeks in the handy sector, where we have seen 4 sales this week, most modern of which NORD SAVANNAH (37K DWT 2013 SAIKI) sold for USD 16.8M.

Gastech offered the industry plenty of opportunities for discussion this week in Singapore. As the week draws to a close, sentiment looks to have the edge with another charterer paying up to cover a Q4 cargo. A reminder to all that the fundamentals (an increasing of available prompt tonnage) and the sentiment don’t need to be aligned for rates to escalate. A key theme of the conference has of course been new business and this week was no different, many new players offered interesting new opportunities in the near term but also from 2027 and beyond. It is clear ambitions, for many, are grand in scope! No newbuilds again this week but let's see if any announcements are made on the back of the remaining meetings this week.

EAST Freight market is staying active despite not even Adnoc dates being published for next month. Although last done for a standard AG voyage at this very moment is just below yesterday baltic print – numbers shown today and last night in the East are now climbing up to the 150s for the early part of October. Charterers with firm cargo dates in the first half, or at least first 10 days, of the month are therefore seemingly rushing to fix in before less ships are available and freight potentially just even higher than as of now.   WEST Entering this week we found the BLPG3 index at mid 190s H/C. Today we find it 25 dollars higher after having seen the last couple deals done at 220 H/C. At the time of writing we have seen about 30 spot fixtures for October dates ex USG/USEC and only a handful of them have been fixed in 2H Oct where we still see several uncovered cargoes left, but the vessel supply is currently very limited this period.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG Thin discussions for evenly split cargos this week and C3/C4 spread narrowed to $3. Oct C3 CP was assessed at $570, Oct/Nov Cp was traded at $15 dollars contango.  Qatar Petroleum was reported to sell a 6-11 Oct lifting full propane cargo on FEI netback. Freight is soaring due to tight fleet and FEI/CP enlarged to $110s from last weeks’ $70s.   FAR EAST Inquiries in window are muted this week as market participants are attending APPEC and Gastech meetings. Off window 23kt propane parcel was bid at Oct FEI plus 3-4 while offered at mid high single digit. Apart from such, 46kt propane for 1h Oct delivery were changed hand between traders at Oct FEI plus mid single digit basis NChina reportedly. A couple of tenders were reported cancelled due to high offers, one is for 23/0 parcel for late Sep/early Oct delivery into Qinzhou, while the other for 11/11 delivered into Shenzhen during Oct. One Cracker user issued tender to buy 22kt or 44kt LPG with butane ratio for Oct delivery. However other Petchem users are hesitant to inquire Oct feedstock, with some considering rate cuts or extend planned turnaround durations. China PP market revived this week as into demanding season, coupled with the impact of stimulus plan on property market over the weekend.
