East of Suez Shipping has come back to life again, with all participants from last week Hong Kong LPG conference now back in their respective offices.  We have seen a handful of deals concluded so far this week, both to Indian Majors and Western traders, and last done now in the high USD 70's pmt excluding awrip.  Going forward we are waiting for pending acceptance dates from Middle Eastern suppliers in August, but we also expect to see few more requirements for July before we close the month.

The overall sentiment in both basins remained steady, but shipping requirements saw a slight decline compared to the previous weeks. The fundamentals of the current trades in both East and West of Suez are still unchanged, as the handful of recent fixtures concluded were intra-basin businesses.  Shipping rates in the Pacific are taking a slight dip and the Atlantic has also seen lesser trades however not enough to justify a drop in rates due to shipping availability being limited and more balanced than the East. Despite the slowdown on the spot, the multi months, term and forward fixing requirements remain fairly strong with Owners standing firm and not submitting to pressure of the current market.  Nevertheless, with Brent prices picking up, more cargo tenders anticipated to come out for Q3-Q4 2019 and seasonal demand in preparation for winter, we expect to see spot activities increase again. Newbuild prices remain unchanged and no further reports of any new orders this week.

text: Mt Belvieu prices are still affected by the weekly stock numbers. This week Mt Belvieu rose after the, 1 million barrel less than expected 1.4million barrel build. International traders cannot ignore the Mt Belvieu price reactions to the weekly inventories, but the feeling is that whether inventories get to 90million or 100million barrels, stocks will be plentiful for winter. Export discussions have been quiet due to an industry conference in Hong Kong and FOB buying ideas have been declining by the day in line with the declining arbs and stagnant freight.

text: MEG: Flat price spiked up from mid-week following the crude price rise, buoyed by the larger decline on crude stock and the concerns on oil supply over the tension between US-Tehran. At the time of writing, Jul CP traded at $376, while Jul FEI at $421. Aug swap number is being volatile, followed tightly at flattish level to July at the moment. But it seems too early to judge if it’s into a contango or backwadation structure, mirroring player’s sentiment on future uncertainties. Jul CP is expected to be announced by this Sunday, and Saudi Aramco is reported to have a mid/2h July lifting 2/2 cargo available.   FAR EAST: With the IHS conference held in HK this week, and the last week before July CP announced, window appears quiet.  On Tue 23kt propane for 1H Aug delivery is traded at Aug FEI plus 1.5$. One fob seller is offering 17-21 Jul lifting 2/2 at discount of 5$, however difficult to entice buyer’s interest as freight still hovering at high 70s level. And propane for 2h Jul was bid at Jul FEI plus $4 while 1h Aug at Aug fei flat only, reflecting the length in in forward market. One North China petchem user have purchased a full propane cargo for 1H Aug delivery reported at CP plus 70s. We expect into Aug China petchem demand to be robust as SP chemical cracker is stockpiling feedstock for the cracker, with all PDHs running at good margin, far better compared to the retailing demand. Indonesia Pertamina issued buy tender for a 3/1 cargo delivered to Kalbut at 9-11th Aug while result was yet to hear. Taiwan FPCC awarded their buy tender for 44kt C3 for 1-10th Aug delivery at Aug MOPJ minus $80.

Some replacing business coupled with a few inquiries are keeping WAF from sliding further right now, but charterers with cargoes off more natural dates have plenty of ships to choose from and we would need an increase in activity in order for rates to hold.

Atlantic and fronthaul going strong on a combination of increased prompt demand and a very limited number of ballasters/early ships, rates for the continent/far east milk routes jumping close to 25 pct and set to continue. We do expect owners to keep pushing for Baltic equivalent rates on Houston/Chiba (via panama) basis, which over the last few days have started to slide. Nevertheless, contrary to the drop in Baltic seen over the last couple of days, a few vessels have reportedly been fixed at rates starting with an 8.

Slightly more bearish undertones for now and increased volumes in all areas required for rates to stabilize.

text: The US supply keeps on coming! Gaining 3.4 million barrel build last week was slightly (around 1 million barrels) above trader expectations. These larger than expected builds and general bearish sentiment in Mt Belvieu has not lead to higher terminalling fee discussions. Skyrocketing freight rates have kept product netback values around 9cpg US-FEI based on flat price. Which in itself is bullish for prompt delivered markets as the arbs are supporting strong freight values from the US. There is trepidation around terminalling fees. Buyers not willing pay… and seller not willing to buy… through flat price values. The trader sentiment is that f it makes sense on paper then it can work. With the outlook for Mt Belvieu prices bearish through high supply. The question is: Does bearish Mt Belvieu lead to a wider arb, and what freight level can it maintain?

text: MEG: Saudi Aramco released their July acceptance over the weekend, with some Butane liftings being advanced. It is reported that the producer is offering equal ratio cargos for July lifting with ample Butane stock. July CP swaps remained flat most of the week, until Thursday afternoon when it rose to $360, shadowing the crude rebound. Not sure if freight has reached the ceiling at $80 but the continuous increment on shipping costs have squeezed the margins, more so when considering current weak demand from India and China. Buyer are asking mid-teens or even higher discounts on FOB.   FAR EAST: Plenty of deals were concluded in the window during this week. 23kt propane for 2h July delivery was traded at Jul FEI plus 3-6$, which equates to July CP plus low mid 50s’. FEI/CP still maintains at 50ish, thanks to the soaring freight. Off window inquiries into China are quite sluggish, thus the spread between US and Non-US origin has been narrowing quickly.   Apart from window deals, a handful of tenders are ongoing. SP Chemical awarded their buy tender to one Chinese major importer at July CP plus 60s for 23k propane, SP Chemicals are reported to be looking for another cargo for end July delivery, for use in their cracker. Following that, Dongguan Juzhengyuan was also reported to have secured Propane from the largest Chinese importer at July CP plus 50s. FPCC awarded their buy tender for 11/11 during 16-20th July delivery into Mailiao at July MOPJ minus mid 80s. Indonesia Pertamina has closed their term tender for 2 full cargos for delivery January to December 2020, result is yet to known.  Having said this, the majority of spot demand is driven by petchem for Propane, buying interest from traditional importers is pretty slim, with only one Chinese importer reported to have purchased an 11/11 cargo at July CP plus around 50$.

The spot shipping market appears to have become subordinate as Charterers have their eyes on the autumn-winter market and in some cases multiyear coverage. Winter coverage often ends up in discussions for a 1yr TC vs the requested 6 or 9 months TC, due to pricing and owners reluctance to take «shoulder months» risk. It will be interesting to see how these year and multiyear discussions pan out over the next few weeks.  Last week was relatively active East of Suez,  but with good availability of vessels, rates remained stable. Markets were quieter West of Suez, but availability within this basin is very limited.  «News of the week» was that Anadarko has taken FID on Mozambique for 12,8 MTPA which could easily translate into a requirement of about 12-16 vessels.

Hostile incidents with ‘attacks’ on tankers in the Meg has created a whole new scenario for the market. Uncertainties of severity was the initial reactions around the word , making charterers with cargoes ready to fix in the Meg to take a step back. Eventually cargoes were fixed and rates have increased some , though not as much as many had thought or even hoped for. The issue of the increased war risk insurance being the most important topic for now. Activity in West Africa , with tonnage supplied from the east , also took a breather but when a fresh fixture was concluded the rate was increased abt 7 ws-points. The Americas with Usg and also Venezuela being the most active load areas has remained active with tonnage much thinner on the ground. Rates also here steadily firming , enticing more owners to start ballasting from the east. Generally firmer undertone throughout for the Vlcc’s.

After ending last week on a negative trend and holidays in Greece on Monday, the trend has continued to be soft. The ECSA market was holding up end of the week, but we now see this market also loosing ground on the rates. The bid/offer gap has widened and fixtures are being done at below last done.  Fhauls are currently paying low USD 16k. TA’s are mid week seeing some slight increase in rates due to less prompt tonnage. The Pacific rounds are continuing to slide and currently trading ard USD 9k.

A rather uneventful start to the week on the Aframax segment both in the North, Mediterranean and Black Sea. Rates have continued it’s downward correction across the board for cross north sea voyages as well as stems from the Baltic. We did see some excitement in the Mediterranean/Black Sea last week with owners being able to put some pressure on freight levels. However a lack of activity along with a long tonnage list have transcended into a softening trend in these areas. We foresee a flat/soft market for the remaining part of the week, but with a healthy program expected from the Black Sea – it might be a turning point for owners trading in the area in the chase for better returns.

East market remains tight as all 1st decade July positions was cleared immediately after Saudi acceptance came out. Now people take a short breather as the Baltic is approaching $80 pmt, after a climb of almost $10 pmt during just one week. The markets further direction will be dictated by inquiries in the middle and second half July, which is yet to hit the market. Looking back at the Baltic history, around $80 was the previous ceiling in 2008, 2011, 2012, 2013 before super bullish cycle came in 2014-2015. Now we are in the time whether this ‘historic’ ceiling works this time again or not. One thing that is different this time is that the previous market movement was made without neo-Panama canal opening and big US export. This time around, the market is mainly driven by widen arb, it would be interesting to see how far Freight is going to go.  Focus in the West VLGC market is on last decade July which is closing in on being wiped out in terms of shipping avails. Thus, in a relatively quiet week in the Western VLGC market, owners look content to see what direction the market will take and seem somewhat hesitant to commit to fixing simply due to some vessel’s discharge schedules are not firm yet. It will be interesting to see whether the Baltic Houston/Chiba equivalent also will face resistance in the coming weeks if the BLPG index flattens out or even starts sliding. As a direct consequence to the market direction over the past few weeks, is time charter requests. We see increased interest in longer-term TCs, and at the same time, we note owners being reluctant to lock in fixed numbers at current levels… We have also seen some activity on the newbuilding scene for the VLGCs, a couple of orders have already been reconfirmed, and at the current moment the Orderbook counts 37 ships. In addition some 6-8 ships are very close to being reconfirmed.

text: MEG: After the large price falls throughout this week, Crude rebounded on Thursday afternoon, trickered by the two tanker explosions in the Gulf of Oman.  Following this, LPG Propane prices rose to $348, reviving a bit from overnight’s slide to below $340.  Butane maintains a discount of about $20 against Propane, which is (still) unusual for a typical summer season. This is a testament to the fact that Butane’s length from producers continue.  With ample supply from Middle East and sluggish demand from end users, July CP is still under pressure. Add to this the seemingly ever increasing freight rates, this has killed many buyers’ appetite, mid-teens discounts appear insufficient to trigger speculative trades as well.  Adnoc released their July acceptances with some liftings being advanced. Qatar Petroleum issued a sales tender for 7-9th July lifting on full propane cargo basis. Saudi Aramco is reported to still have a late June 2/2 cargo available for sale.    FAR EAST: Quiet week with only a few physical deals being concluded this week.  Off window a 23kt Propane cargo for 2h July delivery changed hands at July FEI plus $6-$8, which equates to July CP plus mid high 30s.  Non-US origin equal ratio cargoes are assessed at a similar value, while Propane is still at a premium of plus 50s level, this mainly driven by PDH demand which still enjoy substantial profit margins in an otherwise sluggish market.  The forward traded market into August is currently at a slight backwardation, as the front still gains support due to delays caused by US freeport FM and Nederland turnarounds.  Some players expect the premiums to come off further with the anticipation of plentiful arbitrage cargoes reaching Eastern markets in August, along with cheaper MB price and a perceived weaker demand in the East.

Sentiment changed to a more nervous tone as pacific cargo volumes failed to deliver as expected, however latest activity indicates resistance to further softening. Average daily earnings down some 5 pct w-o-w, to come in at usd 14000, with the two main conference routes waust/china and brazil/china contributing equally much to the slight decline.  Outlook is mixed, as 2 major australian miners have fiscal year ending 30 june and their july volumes could thus be moderate - and coal prices/trades give little reason to cheer, whilst on the other hand numerous vessels busy fitting scrubbers plus the apparent return of brazilian miners to spot scene calls for cautious optimism on the crucial fronthaul trades. Major players keep being busy picking period units, last exemplified by 177000 dwt 2010-built China prompt done for 17-19 months at usd 15500, 177000 dwt 2007-built done for 22-25 months at usd 15300, and 179000 dwt 2010-built rumoured for 6-9 months at usd 15900.

text: Despite strong and increasing  freight, the arb remains open from the US to Europe and Asia. Production and exports remain at record levels and we expect this to continue going forward. In fact it is hard to see the scenario changing anytime soon unless demand begins to waver.  However, with prices so low compared to the alternatives,  this is not something we expect to happen. Propane inventories rose 2.8 million barrels for the week ending June 7th which slightly above trader expectations, and puts the total number on track to reach over 100,000,000 barrels by October 1st , 2019.

A slow start to the week with holidays across many countries in Europe, but with some more activity by mid week. From ECSA vessels are fixing around $ 14000 to Med, similar rates obtained from USG for the same direction. In the Pacific, bad weather has  created problems for several coal producers, leading to several spot vessels in S.Kali and also putting pressure on rates elsewhere in Pacific. Indo/China coal rv's are paying owners around $7000 del Spore. While in the Indian Ocean Safr/WCI paying low $12k + $225k gbb and WCI to Bdesh around mid/high $9000.

A handful of deals were concluded this week for 1st decade July loading in the Middle-East, and the momentum on freight continues. Last deal was reported at $70 pmt (Baltic), and freight is expected to strengthen further as most ships for 1st decade July has already been booked out, while we are still waiting for Aramco July acceptances. Aramco is also being reported selling an FOB cargo in June this week, indicating higher inventory levels, so one could expect more early July nominations once acceptances are out. This could certainly put players without shipping length in a sticky situation. Shipping availability in the west of Suez VLGC market has tightened further and we are faced with basically a handful of vessels until the start of third decade July. The east of Suez market is trading at par with the West and the tight vessel availability should in theory entail a further jump in freight rates from the current Baltic equivalent of USD 110 per ton on Houston/Chiba basis and by the looks of it, we will see fixtures being done north of this level, simply due to tight vessel avails.

The market has turned down in both basins this week, with the TA-rates especially taking a major hit. A transatlantic round voyage currently yields around USD 7,000 per day, while a short fronthaul from the continent yields something the middle of USD 16,000. In the east, a Pacific round voyage now pays around the USD 10,000's per day. The BPI 4TC-index is down 155 points for the week, currently at 1149.

text: Propane inventories resumed their seasonable build , increasing this week by 2.3 million barrels. At this pace inventories should peak at over 100 million barrels by the end of September. This level should ensure more than enough inventory to support a cold winter, as well as maximum exports,  even with the export expansion at Enterprise which will come on line in the third quarter. This high inventory level is also effecting prices, pushing propane levels down to less than 35 percent of WTI. This normally is good for the Arb however high freights are hampering US Gulf exports. In South America, Brazilian demand continues at their normal winter pace.

text: MEG: This last week have seen a nose dive in prices of LPG from the MEG. It started almost to the minute of June LPG CP prices being announced, by Crude falling sharply on the last trading last week, only to fall even more Monday of this week. While the fall in Crude prices have been sharp, equaling nearly 13 pct. The drop in LPG prices have been even larger, using July’s traded CP over the same period, equaling about 17 pct. We are today in a situation where the traded July Propane CP is at 343, June CP confirmed at 430, this means that the market expect Propane CP to drop by a massive 20 pct. The spot physical price have dropped even more with close to a handful of deals done at discount to July CP. The discounts ranged from high single digit to high teens. The Butane price have been hit ever harder than Propane and it seems that this pricing trend is set to continue with the market being awash with Butane right now.   FAR EAST: The pricing trend in the Eastern markets have mirrored that seen in MEG. While window deal(s) have been near absent this week, one was done earlier today where a Marcus Hook 23/00 1h July was confirmed at July FEI +6, a number of physical deals was confirmed. Market chatter refers to 1 cargo of 22+22 to East China and another of 11+11 to a similar destination with arrival 2nd hf July was concluded at equivalent of July CP netbacks in the minus 30’s and a 22+22 kt cargo for arrival SE Asia early July was heard done at equivalent of July FOB minus mid teens. It feels like end users are taking this opportunity to fill their storages with cargo at time when prices are perceived to have reached bottom, or near thereto. Sellers have had to play ball as the high freights have made it financially impossible to sit vessels and hope for higher prices, at today’s Baltic the VLGC cost of sitting just 1 day is in excess of USD 1.25 PMT. For Propane there are some relief with Propylene trading at close to USD 1,000 PMT in the East and Propane being landed considerably below USD 500 PMT, very large margins are being achieved by the PDH plant operators and we have now seen such operators tendering for cargoes with arrival from end June till end July.  With US volumes seeing an even larger FOB price adjustment, it will be interesting to see where this market will take us in the next 1 to 2 months.

The Aframax market in the North Sea and Baltic has been flat all week on the back of ships going short and discharging in Baltic area. TD7 and TD17 have been held steady at WS100 and WS72.5 respectively throughout the week, and owners have opted for cargoes with quick turnaround as they wait for activity levels to pick up. In the Mediterranean and Black Sea, we have seen the rates drop close to 30 world scale points over the course of the week, as a downward correction takes form. While prompt ships are piling up in the area, the lack of activity from charterers is making it difficult for owners to keep the pressure on rates. At the time of writing, a cross-Med voyage stands at about WS80, giving owners a TCE close to USD 7,000 per day. In the week to come we expect freight levels in the Mediterranean and Black Sea to remain under pressure as the current tonnage list still looks healthy.

Suezmaxes have seen a good level of activity over the last week. The tonnage overhang on early dates have started to clear up and rates are on the move as such. East of Suez rates are still soft as handicapped tonnage are fighting for employment, keeping rates at last done levels with little prospect of any swift recovery.

A quiet week due to holidays and Nor-Shipping, with a market slightly down in both hemispheres. A transatlantic round voyage currently yields about USD 10,000 per day, while a short fronthaul from the Continent yields something the middle of USD 18,000. In the East, a Pacific round voyage now pays around the USD 10,000's per day. The BPI 4TC-index is down 33 points for the week, currently at 1304 points.

Slightly better times for the big ships, mainly due to Australian iron ore miners enjoying good prices and exporting at max capacity prior to end of fiscal year. Chinese inventories are moderate/low thus this development is expected to continue, and with major Brazilian miner Vale now back on stage taking ships for July loading prospects are positive. Ever more units about to disappear 30-40 days for scrubber fitting, contributing to a robust supply/demand ratio. In numbers, average daily earnings for standard 180k dwt's are up around 7 pct w-o-w to come in at USD 15k. Voyage rates only marginally up, meaning spot improvement includes lower bunker prices not being factored in. Major takers busy picking period units, last exemplified by 2009-built 180k dwt delivering China prompt for short period at USD 18k - for 12 months and longer levels still hover around USD 16-16,500 on such units.

There are very few bright spots anywhere for the VLCCs and it has not been for some time. The market remains ‘overtonnaged’ virtually for all the major VLCC-routes. There is however a feeling that we are at the bottom, but the long awaited uptick in rates and earnings appear to be later than most had both hoped and expected. There has been a few moments where owners have tried to push rates up, just a little, but without much success. The general volumes of business for the major VLCC-routes are far from thin, but for now insufficient to change the oversized tonnage-list. Therefore more of the same to come with subdued rates as we approach the summer.

The momentum in the freight market from last week has continued into this week, and shipping availability for current fixing window i.e. end June remains relatively tight. Most of the activity has been on the back of shipping demand from Indian majors, and last done rates are now trailing in the USD high 60s pmt Baltic. Going forward we are waiting for July acceptances from most of the Middle Eastern suppliers, and we expect the market to cool off a little bit in the coming days.  Although there has been some inquiries and some fixing activity too, the VLGC market in the western hemisphere has to be described as somewhat subdued this week. At least so for the beginning of the week, as we do now see some increased interest. Levels discussed so far this week, indicate that the western market is trading with a small premium to the Eastern Baltic benchmark, although not more than say 2-3% at the time of writing. We do believe this will carry on, as there are some uncovered cargoes out of the US Gulf during 1st half of July, and vessel supply is generally tight.

Supramax sentiment has seen healthy upturn in Atlantic Basin. Rates on Supramaxes for USG/Cont-Med seen stable about USD 14k, Ultramaxes were fixing low USD 20k. The ECSA market stabilized with firm rates which are the best so far during this year. Supras and Ultras reported USD 15k for trip via ECSA to Cont/Med and FH at USD 13.5k+USD 350k bb. Cont and Med markets were stable with rates for India reporting USD 14-15k. Far East Pacific rates were facing a negative trend, and rates were falling further about USD 1k/d lower from last week. On the Pacific round Tess52 delivering CJK rates were reported about USD 7k/d. Ultra reported was fixed at USD 8.5 for a trip dop Singapore via Australia to China. Indo coal also seen negative development and owners had to face lower rates.

The LNG spot market continues to delight buyers and dismay sellers, with delivered cargo pricing slipping further in Europe and hitting a [3]-year low in the Far East. On-shore storage remains high and the East/West arbitrage is firmly shut, leading to fewer fresh requirements and the squeezing of trading margins. The prompt shipping market has in turn ceased strengthening and may be moving towards a shallow decline: the few recent fixtures completed suggest a slight drop in headline rates, albeit with overall structures that retain elements of positioning and repositioning. However, the view is quite different further out, as the relatively weak hands held by LNG sellers and shipowners today may herald a loaded deck tomorrow. The longer-term ton-mile story remains strong: the first cargo has left Cameron and Prelude is expected to follow suit imminently with more to come, and there is plenty of growth potential offered by an average voyage distance today that is down 10% against long-term levels. Add in to the mix a few other “ifs” and “maybes” that the present market has produced, such as the scope for floating storage if the market enters a contango or for reloads out of a full Europe if the arbitrage opens wide, and the firm and strengthening sentiment of owners towards longer-term charters makes sense.

text: MEG: The highlight of the week was the announcement of Saudi Contract Prices for June of $430 for Propane and $415 for Butane. At the time of announcement, this was more or less in line with expectations. However, as the week have moved on, it become obvious that there are/were substantial unsold FOB volumes still to be placed. These volumes are from producers and from traders as well Some of these have now been cleared but at large discounts to CP, ranging from high single digit to high teen’s. This price dive has been aided by the continued strength in the VLGC freights. Arriving in the office Monday morning, we were presented with a near contango situation for the balance of the year but this quickly changed whereby backwardation has once again reared it’s ugly head, especially so for Butane. It is reported that Iran LPG export volumes this month will reach 550 kt, or more.   FAR EAST: It has not really been an active trading week, tough some deals were concluded. A WAF origin cargo was sold into East China for 1st half July arrival and a window deal for 23 kt c3 1st half June at June FEI plus 8 was done. These deals are more or less representative of the market developments this week. While these deals point to a CP netback of lower than minus 20, it should not surprise anyone that this downward pressure on CFR values more than likely will continue for some time. The realization that slowing increase in demand from the 2 biggest import markets, combined with continued strong Iranian exports and new volumes from US, Canada and Australia, mean that Eastern markets are very well supplied.

WEST  Shipping markets in the West has continued firming this week with freight rates now being concluded in the low USD 100’s pmt East and mid USD 50’s pmt West for end June and early July loadings.  The position list is dominated by the main Owners for 1st decade July so we expect freight to remain tight. The current high earnings for Owners seen over the last couple of months has caught the whole market by surprise, and nobody anticipated that we could be seeing above USD 1.5 million per month. But as long as the US Gulf terminals are experiencing challenging conditions with large delays, shipping will remain tight and freight rates will stay strong. Focus is now on 1st decade July as June is close to fully booked.  EAST East shipping availability is tight for June. A couple inquiries in 2nd decade June and some MEG FOB tenders received some attention. Thus, Baltic is now back to above the USD 60 pmt mark. We start to see more trader re-lets in 3rd decade June and subsequently, the question is how many cargoes are left for end June.

It has been a week with healthy activity in all areas for Suezmaxes. Activity in the Americas have picked up again after being idle for a few weeks - a much needed addition for Suezmaxes trading in the Atlantic. Despite a good level of fixing activity, the rates have been moving sideways, at best, with owners still struggling to clear out the tonnage overhang in West Mediterranean and West Africa following a busy period on VLCCs. With rates for round voyages in the Atlantic barely covering OPEX, there is a limited downside for the owners to rather wait instead of fixing.

We are a few days away from June, which will mark the beginning of the Northern Hemisphere summer months. Although we are only reaching the opening of the summer ‘’peak’’ demand period, it is already proving to be a quite different setup for this summer in the LNG market compared to same time last year, predominantly driven by the sluggish cargo demand and ample supply, pushing the LNG prices close to annual lows. This seems to have caught up with the prompt spot LNG shipping market too as we have recorded only a handful of fresh requirements across the basins, halting the hike of the freight rates for now. Shipping availability has also increased, as we have seen a number of sublets appearing, possibly putting some pressure on the spot freight rates in the upcoming weeks. It is quite a different story on term requirements however, as owners are still holding on to their strong views about the second half of this year, supported by the fact that we see a steady flow of interest for multi-month charters from different LNG players and expect more LNG volume to come online. On the newbuilding front, Hyundai Heavy Industries confirmed late last week to have secured an order for two 180kcbm LNGC newbuilds, increasing the order tally for 2019 to a total of 22.

text: The US propane inventories showed an unexpected drawdown today of 100,000 barrels. This drawdown was completely unexpected and very far from the consensus view of a build of 2 million barrels. Under normal circumstances,  this would have caused the propane market to spike upwards but with crude falling so fast and so hard it meant that propane would not fall as much and propane did firm compared to WTI closing today at 39 percent of WTI. General belief is that that this is a correction from prior weeks and that next week should once again show a build of close to 2 million barrels. Bottom line is that there is enough inventory to support, domestic cracking, retail and exports for the foreseeable future. In other news US terminals are continuing their catch up from last months delays. Enterprise expects to be caught up in early June and Targa by late June. In Canada, Alta Gas completed their first export from their new facility at Prince Rupert Island, British Colombia. They had a few normal start up delays but overall the terminal performed well and the spec was perfect. All going well Alta gas hopes to have 30 VLGC propane cargos a year from the new terminal.

text: The propane market for sure did not like the stats this week and combined with falling crude oil, made for an ugly day losing over 2.25 CPG. Overall propane inventories are getting rather high @ 65.8 million 48 of which is in the Gulf Coast.    FOB USGC terminalling fees are bid at 7.5cpg while offers are in the double digits for June cargoes. This wide bid/offer level is attributed to window premiums in the East market. These cash premiums remain in the single digits at the moment. This means that traders are reluctant to sell FOB US at a flat netback US/FEI levels. One thing is for , sure as long as market remains in backwardation l, stock building will not start and the entire market knows it must before the winter season.

text: MEG: Another volatile week as flat values continued sliding, following the crude.  June propane CP is now trading at $424 at the time of writing, almost $100 less than May CP. Butane is traded at $18 less.  KPC is reportedly awarded their 4/5th June 2/2 at June CP minus mid high single digit.  Qatar tendered to sell a 3/1 for 26/28th June lifting at the pricing on BL dates, with the backwardation to July CP being at more than teens this doesn’t look attractive to buyers unless it comes with an attached substantial discount, more so considering the high freight and sluggish demand in Eastern CFR markets.    FAR EAST: Premiums has come off quickly this week as US export resumes operation and supply tensions getting eased. On Thursday a handful of deals was concluded in the window. 23k propane for 2h June delivery was traded at June FEI plus $11 and July FEI plus $12, while similar cargo for 1h July was done at July FEI plus $6, which reveals the forward length.  There are some cargos being placed into China at a lower premium this week. Market appears long with abundant equal ratio cargos, some of which being surplus from India importers. Propane is maintaining it’s higher value with requirement from PDH buyer. 23k propane was sold at June CP plus low 50s while 11/11 was done at $15-20 lower. One domestic importer is reported to have resold a 2/2 cargo for 2h June delivery at June CP plus 30s level.  Indonesia’s Pertamina appear to have awarded their two 2/2 cargoes for July delivery at June CP plus high 20s to low 30s.  FPC awarded their spot tender for a 33/11 cargo delivered during 1st half July at July MOPJ minus around $105. Previously they’ve awarded their term tender reported at MOPJ minus 70s for 44k C3 monthly from July 2019 to June 2020.

This segment is not yet in equilibrium, but present moderate but positive developments for the big ships nevertheless appear robust. Average spot earnings up 5 pct w-o-w coming in at USD 12300/day, mostly due to Australian iron ore exporters being busy and increasing period appetite amongst major players. The effect of hundreds of units disappearing from spot scene for 1-1.5 months each to fit scrubbers/wbts before deadline now starts to kick in, and an expected return of crucial Brazilian iron ore export capacity may add fuel to an impending fire come summer/autumn. Representative period fixtures include 177000/2005 with end-year drydock coming up reportedly done basis spot delivery Japan for 16-20 months at around USD 15500.

The Pacific market was stable this week with a slow start due to the holiday in Singapore on Monday.  Indo coal was fixing close to 8,000 from south China.  The USG/USEC market was firming up slowly, with more cargoes available in the area.  Petcoke to Med was fixed at USD 14,000 and to India USD 18,000. The ECSA market is still steadily increasing. Tess 58’ is able to obtain 15,000 + for Med and trip to Singapore -Japan paying close to 13500 plus 350,000 BB. Cont is showing little demand and over supply of tonnage which is pressuring rates. FH from Baltic to India pays low USD 12,000.

We have seen increased activity on shipping East of Suez on the back of June Aramco acceptances that was posted last week. Several ships were booked for 1H June loading in the mid/high usd 50s Baltic, and freight going forward is certainly more bullish as vessel availability remains fairly tight. Owners ideas for next fixing window ie 2H June is moving towards usd 60+, and it will be interesting to see if/when any deals get booked out at these levels. On a week-on-week basis the Baltic rate have moved up with about USD 4.4 pmt, representing an increase in the Time charter equivalent (T/C/E) rates of about 4,500 per day. The Western VLGC market remains tight on vessel supply for June out of the US Gulf. Freight rates bottomed out in the mid/low USD 90’s per ton (Houston/Chiba via Panama) and parallel to a rising Baltic, we expect that owners’ rate ideas will keep increasing. As a result of the Baltic jump, the East and West markets are currently trading at par. The US Gulf is still experiencing significant delays.

Rates continued to edge upwards this week with a small yet persistent increase. Demand for cargo appears to have waned again and it’s become quite apparent that freight rates have begun their own journey and delinked from cargo prices. This lack of correlation between the cargo and freight market is highly irregular and has many market players perplexed when assessing multi-month indications. A small yet significant shopping spree for Q3 and Q4 cover has occurred over the past couple of weeks and has left less than a handful of different Owners with flexible tonnage available for the course of 2019. Although the number of multi-month fixtures this year is less when compared to 2018, it is worth noting that this time last year marked the commencement of Charterers taking winter coverage and what followed was a rapid change in the freight market. Cargo prices last summer where very different to today’s but with European regasification slots filling up fast it could be ton-time that dominates the headlines this summer. Availability remains fair with sufficient vessels to serve anticipated demand on the prompt but with more commissioning cargoes coming online in the near future this landscape is likely to change. New build prices take a tick up to 189 this week although orders through Q2 have been slower than the past two quarters.

Overall, last week was all about absorbing the overhang of tonnage than anything else and this week looks like will be much the same. The level of activity generally is high which helps trimming lenghty position lists, we need this activity to continue before we see any uptick in rates – market is very much flat.

Earnings are still barely covering opex, however activity in the West and predominantly in the USG area has attracted a handful eastern ballasters for the next fixing window to come, early July. Market steady for now, but owners seem more optimistic as we are entering the summer months.

In Se Asia, the market was softening. Indo/China coal RV trading around USD 9,000 bss S.China delivery, while Aussie RV to China paying around USD 10,500 bss Singapore delivery.

This volatile segment is trying to find a clear direction from the present USD 12,000/day earnings for standard units. General expectations are for recovery and a stronger development going forward, but underlying trade war tensions combined with uncertain reliability of Brazilian iron ore exports make nervous market players take one day at a time. Increasing fronthaul and transatlantic volumes have so far resulted in a 20 pct w-o-w jump in value for the Continent-Brazil-China trade coming in at Usd 25,400/day. Mixing the signals is the West Australia/China iron ore conference trade at healthy volumes, but status quo moneywise at USD 6.25 pmt or around USD 11,500/day on good units. Period interest amongst major operators is good and growing, last exemplified with very mediocre 180,000 dwt/built 2006 delivering China prompt for about a year at around USD 15,500/day.

A positive week in both hemispheres, where especially the grain market from ECSA has shown a solid increase in rates. A transatlantic round voyage currently pays owners about USD 10,500 per day, while a short fronthaul from the Continent yields about USD 18,000. In the East, a Pacific round voyage pays around the mid USD 8,000's. The BPI 4TC-index is currently at 1243 points, up 55 points from last week.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: Delays , delays, delays. Seems the Houston Ship Channel cannot rid itself from the huge magnitude of delays that have occurred this year. First it was fog, then two terrible explosions at two different locations, and last week a collision between a tanker and several barges. The effects of these delays had huge ramifications in the Asian markets and the effects of which are still being felt. Asia is now very dependent on US exports and delays in the US Gulf result in large premiums being paid in Asia. The Asian market is also complicated by the 25 percent tariffs on US product going into China  which has in turn put a premium on non US origin product. On the domestic front the US Propane market showed a weekly build of 2.7 million barrels the majority of which was in the US Gulf. Production came in well over 2 million  barrels per day and domestic demand showed an all time low. Going forward we expect lower US prices and the arb to remain wide.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG: Saudi Aramco released their June acceptances, and it appears that there are some shortage on C3 supply. Lifters who have full C3 liftings get delays while the rest with equal ratios are more comfortable with dates as per nominated. There are plenty of equal ratio cargoes are available in the FOB market and the offer level for 2h June lifting has come off to discount level.  KPC issued a sales tender for a 4/5 June lifting 2/2 c3/c4, result is not known yet.  Indian importers are also reported to postpone/resell some June lifting FOBs.  Paper swap values have been volatile this week. US stock buildup and higher production figures than expected has smashed the market values.  June CP once traded at $480 earlier this week, only to plunge below $450$ and then slightly rebound to $455 at time of writing. Butane is assessed $22 cheaper but with the length on Butane we expect the spread to expand.  FAR EAST: Due to the minor delays caused by the collision in Houston ship channel over the weekend, the June CFR market has tightened, buyers has been buying in/off window to cover front shorts. 23kt propane for 1h June was traded in window at June FEI plus $53, last time such a high premium was achieved is two years back.  2h June CFR market is less tight but Japanese buyers are actively covering in at levels of June FEI plus $25-30.  Comparatively, China importers have been less active this week, main buyers have been PDH operators. Sluggish demand from the domestic sector is killing extra speculative interest. Traditional importers are cautiously monitoring their inventories and sales before deciding whether to buy additional tons, taking into consideration the front premium and intermonth spread between June/July.

The VLGC market in the East has been in a waiting mode for the Saudi cargo acceptances this week. And with this inactivity, the market has gradually gone through some downward adjustments on rates. The Baltic VLGC rates have come down almost 3 dollars over the week and are at the current moment trading just below 40,000 per day. We expect the market sentiment to change once the mentioned cargo acceptances are out as this will most probably take out a few vessel positions and further reduce the vessel length for June loading, which are already significantly shorter due to Indian congestion and consequential vessel delays there. As such we do expect the 14-day consecutive drop in the Baltic will come to an end and flatten out.  In the Western market a number of ships has being taken out for June loadings, both out of USG and USEC. The majority of fixtures have been concluded at around mid USD 90’s East and in the low USD 50’s West, however, in the short term going forward, freight looks set to increase as vessel supply is tight. The Houston ship channel experienced a collision between a VLGC and two barges, resulting in a spillage and consequently closure of both inbound and outbound vessel traffic. Nevertheless, no major effects from the collision has been observed so far and we expect any delays to be back on time by next week.

The Suezmax market showed some limited signs of life over the past week’s 3rd decade. West Africa dates were shown in sparse volumes with Nigerian grades still seemingly out of favour with European refiners, rates are currently scraping along the bottom. There were some signs of date sensitivity towards end month, but that seems to have dissipated. In the Mediterranean, there are still cargoes moving out of Libya even though the current political situation is very fragile. Very little action to report out of the Black Sea, with owners having very little to get their teeth into. The rates have been softening down to ws75 currently for TD6, with earnings now down below 10k per day.  The immediate market outlook seems to have a softer trend for the week ahead.

A very active week for the VLCCs, to say the least. The May MEG program was lagging but has caught up with the monthly count creeping towards 130, which is close to a normal month. Optimism did rise among owners when the June cargoes emerged earlier than customary. The result however is hardly what owners were looking for as rates have only strengthened marginally as tonnage remain in abundance. Wafr and USG East remain flat as well, despite fierce attempts from owners. The general optimism for the summer and early autumn remains in force, but the general volumes for all the major VLCC routes have to increase and continue over time to change much from present levels and earnings. The bottom, however, appears to be history and things are more likely to strengthen, though slowly.

Over the past week, LNG Shipping rates have been strengthening on basic market fundamentals, both east and west of Suez. We have seen tightness on modern tonnage and in addition to firmer rates, ballast bonus sentiment is close to roundtrip economics. However, the cross-basin arb is still very much closed. The question therefore is, will this firmer trend continue through the summer and into the autumn or will we have a repeat of last year’s development, where spot rates increased in June, but came of slightly ahead of August?   Going forward, there are quite a few scheduled redeliveries where some need to drydock, but they are also getting good attention from charterers for potential autumn/winter coverage.    DSME logged one LNGC NB this week, although it’s a little uncertainty around the price, it appears to have been a slot that was priced some time ago.

Aframax rates in the North Sea and Baltic increased end of last week, with main routes picking up around 15 points. Main driver for this was the large Baltic crude program combined with the disturbance around the Ust-Luga oil being contaminated with organic chlorides. However, the situation is seemingly under control again. However, some of the vessels that have loaded in Ust-Luga will be discharging in the Baltic area. This means that there will be a lot of available tonnage for forward dates in the Baltic. So, we expect to see a significant downward correction in the natural fixing window, despite of a quite decent volume of cargoes. The Mediterranean and Black Sea market has traded sideways the past week, as owners take a stand in order to maintain or improve the current rate levels. At time of writing TD19 stands at ws107.5, giving owners returns around USD 15,000 per day. A positive note is that there has been a bit more traction in the US Gulf area, which may be an attractive market for owners to re-position their ships to.

However owners resistance started to build in West Africa with some preferring to stand off cargoes preferring to sit and wait for the right voyages, this has had a knock on effect with ws 80 now having been paid for waf/east up a handful of points but purely being sentiment driven. Elsewhere the Med and Black sea have ben low on fixing volume with TD6 currently steady at ws 80 no too much will change here for the balance of this week.

Another lacklustre week in the VLCC market, with ships piling up in Fujairah and Galle. Owners are currently facing returns well below OPEX for most cargo combinations, with rates currently trading in the high W30’s from both MEG- and West Africa/eastbound for modern ships – and a 2.5-5 point discount for older units.

After the last week's declining market levels, we saw an increase in activity today with some C5 fixtures concluded in the mid-6 range.  FFAs has continued to push upwards the last few days in spite of the Trump announcement and the recent shutdown in steel capacity in China in view of the holidays.  The Atlantic seems tighter on prompt dates going forward, which gives cause for optimism on the near term market outlook.

Aframaxes trading in the North Sea and Baltic have seen healthy activity levels this week, with owners continuously pushing to keep this positive momentum going. With TD7 currently trading around WS 115 levels, we expect a firm sentiment in the natural fixing window in the North. Owners are finally seeing alternatives in surrounding markets which have picked up, such as the Mediterranean and Black Sea, where we have seen an firm upward trend in freight levels. Returns for a TD19 voyage have picked up over the week, from around USD 1000 pd mid last week to USD 12000 pd at time of writing. TD19 currently stands at WS 100. Fresh cargoes have been coming into the market keeping activity levels firm. At the moment owners are finding this a an attractive market to be in and we are expecting them to maintain their stand in the week to come in order to ensure further uptick in freight rates.

With last weeks holidays in the east and the UK-holiday on Monday, the market has remained quite flat in both hemispheres. With the latest increase in tariffs imposed on China by the Trump-administration, many expect China to take on countermeasures shortly - which obviously can affect the market negatively. A transatlantic round voyage currently pays owners about USD 10,000 per day, while a short fronthaul from the continent yields about USD 17,000. In the east, a Pacific round voyage pays around the low USD 8,000's. The BPI 4TC-index is currently at 1188 points.

It has been quite an active week for LNG Shipping. Spot hire rates have increased on the back of several cargoes / requirements in both basins. In addition to the rise in rates, there is a significant push from Owners to cover fuel cost on positioning, as well as improvements on ballast bonus figures. The availability list has also seen a reduction; however, we are far from being “short” shipping, but rather «balanced» as we currently do not foresee any big challenges for Charterers looking to secure a ship for 1H June. Also, due to a weak JKM index versus a steadier NBP, the arbitrage to the East has been closed for quite some time and with most cargoes trading intra basin, ships that are fixed are likely to return to the market shortly. Nonetheless, the current situation looks to favor Owners and we may see the spot market firming further.       Newbuild prices remain unchanged and no further reports of any new orders this week.

A couple of vessels were fixed ex US East Coast for loading in the beginning June at the end of last week, otherwise, it has been fairly inactive. Last week’s notion we made about the freight market struggling to find its feet, eventually saw a seemingly established floor of mid USD 90’s per ton Houston/Chiba via Panama for 1st decade June loaders ex US. A relatively short position list up to around 10th June leaves hopes that freight may remain in this region going forward.  VLGC shipping market East of Suez remains quiet, and the only real requirement seen (HPCL 23-24 May ex Ras Laffan) was eventually withdrawn. We do however expect to see more interest from Indian Charterers later in May, as congestion in India continues and hence their TC ships might run late. Otherwise shipping availability for next fixing window i.e. 2nd half May remains healthy, and one would expect next deal to be done at discount to Baltic. Most players are still not in a rush to do anything though, and also awaiting pending June acceptances from Adnoc and Aramco which should set the tone for end May/early June.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: Exports from the US have maintained above 1.3million barrels per day. Market participants sees this level as the new normal at least until the EPD expansion comes on line with 7 more cargos per month in September. The arbs remain wide enough to sustain strong freight levels both to Europe and the East. South American demand continues it’s seasonal rise.   On the domestic front the build of 1.1million barrels was smaller than the expected 1.5 range though overall inventories are still over 22 million higher then this time last year. Most of the builds recently have been in the Midwest which may cause some more downward pressure there as the spread between Midwest and USGC is about 6cpg but some of the other products are 10cpg or higher. The outright price has not moved very much this week on the front with 1cpg change week on week from the high to the low. The average for the week on front month has been 58.8125-59.0625, with the high being after stats came out. Also of note the prices are at or close to the lows for the last 11 months. On the Butane front the price had largely been following crude oil and has seen a little more volatility with a weekly range on the front of 63- 66.0625 for the daily average. Volumes have been fairly lackluster on the front trades.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG: Earlier this week May Propane CP has been under downward pressure at 430ish and rebounded mid- week. At the time of writing, May CP is traded at 450$. However, butane CP value has dropped significantly and traded at $15 less than propane, which is irregular in a summer season. One main reason is less demand from both Indian and China, and the other being more Us butane into east available now.    FAR EAST:  1H/2H June backwardation is widening. Bids for 23kt propane for 1h June delivery has edging up to June FEI plus 37$ on Thurs window while no offer seen. While off window 2h June delivery cargos were reported done at June FEI plus mid-teens. On Wed a non-Us 22/22 split cargo for 2h June delivery is traded at flat price of 494$, equates to May CP plus mid low 50s, which has surprised players as initially some sellers asking at a premium of 70s for cargos sale into China. Premium has come off rapidly and a couple of cargos have been placed into China. 11/11 for 1h June delivery is reported concluded at May CP plus mid low 50s while propane a few bucks more.   Taiwan CPC issued buy tender for 22kt equal ratio cargo during 21-30 June delivery. The result is yet to know. FPC has issued buy term tender for 22-44k C3 delivered from July 2019 to June 2020.   The escalating China-Us trade tension is another focus of this week, and stock/commodity market have been very volatile. Players are cautiously waiting for official results on Friday, although most not really anticipate for a positive result according to latest reactions.

In general, both east and west of Suez has been quiet over the last week. Freight rates are struggling to find their feet and as a result, we are now seeing Baltic quoted sub USD 60 per ton and it is expected a further drop in the short term. Before long, early June fixing ex USG will kick off, however, rates are expected to drop somewhat from last done of USD 100 per ton.

Firstly, thanks to all readers for completing the information request sent out last week, it’s great to have such a strong response and an active audience. Enough of the admin, the LNG freight market has more than enough going on to fill this column despite numerous public holidays worldwide. Live tenders from CFE and Gail this week have caused a spur of activity in and around the Americas. Across the Atlantic, West Africa has also had its fair share of available cargoes just as the first production from Argentina looks to be hitting the market. When considered with the Algerian and Egyptian volumes seen over the recent weeks and the imminent US commissioning volumes due, the Atlantic has never been so dynamic in terms of production. It’s not quite as positive on the demand side with the Atlantic to Pacific arb struggling to support consistent cross basin trade flow. The Pacific remains a little muted with limited fixtures being reported and as we increase the ballast bonus sentiment, it is the Pacific that weighs on the assessment advancing further this week. No reported new build orders this week but some long term tenders are progressing well which should see the total tally of uncommitted vessels on order book reduce. Happy holidaying if you are out of the office this week.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG: Saudi Aramco set their May Contract Prices for Propane at $525$, up by $10 and for Butane at $530, down by $5. Although it was in line with the swap values, some players now say the contract price is higher than their expectations, more so as crude has softened this week.  Qatar Petroleum released their June acceptances with only a few delays, most lifters got dates as per nomination. June CP has seen a mini crash, so now standing at $450 at the time of writing, equal to a 14 pct drop as compared to May. Butane saw a even larger drop in prices. June CP may yet rebound, as Iran sanctions starts to take effect but so far the slow demand from India and perceived sufficient supply from US have suppressed the price.   FAR EAST:  The market is quiet due to Japan Golden Week and China Labour Day celebrations.  Few bids and offers are shown in the window, with 23kt C3 for 1h June bid at June FEI plus $13/14 and no offers seen, at the same time 2h June Sellers are asking May FEI level minus $1.  With the US terminal backlocks being slowly cleared, players anticipate that the 2h June market will be sufficiently supplied with cargoes and premiums will come off.  China imported 4.67mmt LPG in Q1, slightly less by than same period in 2018 by 2 pct, this is despite China now has one additional PDH plant which commenced operations during Feb 2019. Currently China’s domestic market price is under pressure with disappointing margins from both residential and petchem sectors is seen. In addition the summer season is soon upon us, combined with disappointing Propylene demand and lower Gasoline additives margins. Even so, China importers have started exploring the June market with expectations that premiums coming off with softening freight and overall ample supply.  China based LPG Buyers still have to cope with the uncertainty on US-China tariff talks, positive signals have been released in recent talks and people expects something progressive will come out soon.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: The US market has shifted into Spring and Summer mode leaving the fears of running out of product behind. Now the sentiment has shifted to  the discussion of can the rest of the world take all the US exports?  During the Enterprise conference call yesterday their CEO referred to how high prices create supply and low prices create demand, and the US market seems to be in the sweet spot of creating supply and demand. This,  we agree with,  and with the Mt Belvieu propane price around 40 percent of WTI, we see the arb being open and exports continuing at a very high level. In fact exports for last week were seen at record levels.  Also during the conference call  Enterprise confirmed their expansion is on schedule and additional exports will commence during the 3rd quarter of this year.

After c5 bottomed at USD 5.35 last week, the market has improved to 6.15 this week on the back of fresh enquiries out of Australia. There also been more period activity with modern 180,000 units being paid 16,300 and 17,000 for one year. In the near term we expect the market to improve a bit further, but the big gains have to wait until we see stronger activity out of Brazil. In that respect, things are of course hinging on how quickly Vale can bring capacity back online.

Optimisation is the name of the game for those players with a fleet of LNG vessels. Portfolio players constantly optimise their fleets to charter in whenever it is more economical to do so, whilst spare vessels, usually with short term availability, are marketed for third party charter and this goes someway to explaining the number of vessels chalked up on the position list. Despite the number of chartering enquiries, rates remain depressed as competition remains high with shipowners eager to ensure that their vessels are moving. There are various cargoes available in the Pacific basin and they are set to keep chartering activity at a moderate level but some way off those previously witnessed. With new US volumes due to come online in the coming months and the hope of a warm start to summer, Owner's eyes are on charter hire rate levels with the hope of tightening in the shipping market. In reality this could be some months off but on the flip-side sublets are a high percentage of the availability and can vanish with little warning. Worldwide availability looks relatively balanced albeit oversupplied as intra-basin trade continues to be the overwhelming route choice.     The Atlantic basin has been relatively quiet of late but we expect some vessels to be fixed given the ongoing good production out of North Africa. Spot trades from the Atlantic to the Far East are still a rarity with the abundance of cargoes from South East Asia and Australia providing any Far East LNG purchase interest with an obvious choice of source for any required cargoes.

SE Asia market has seen good improvement due to the Indonesian coal export. Levels increased to 9,000/10,000 pd. Ultramax was fixed USD mid 12,000 pd for a trip to East Coast India from Singapore. South African trip into China was reported at around USD 12,000 pd plus 200k ballast bonus, which is also better than last done. Continental seen healthy enquiry of fertiliser stems to ECSA and Far East. USG experienced balanced market, and stable rates.  USG trip into Mediterranean was reported at USD 12,750 pd on an Ultramax and FH with Petckoke to India USD 19,000. ECSA seen good demand for prompt tonnage and rates improved. ECSA to Mediterranean fixing at 14,000 on Supra and USD 17,000 in Ultra.

With rates continuing to improve, especially in the Atlantic, the BPI 4TC-Index has risen this week, now at 1177 points.  A transatlantic round voyage currently yields about USD 10,000 per day, while a short fronthaul from the Continent yields around low USD 17,000. In the East, a Pacific round voyage pays around USD 8,000.

WEST: Focus in the West is still on end May ex USG, which is tight on vessel supply simply due to all the forward fixing done over the last couple of weeks. Having said that, the Baltic has rallied and the equivalent rate for Houston/East voyages is now up to about USD 105 per ton basis Houston/Chiba via Panama, whereas last confirmed fixture ex Houston to go East was actually in the high USD 80’s per ton. There are still a couple of (potentially) uncovered stems end May in the USG, although charterers’ rate ideas and owners’ ideas are, time being, too far apart. Early June fixing has yet to kick off.  EAST: Most of the 1st half May positions in the MEG were covered during last week, and while shipping availability was fairly tight for same period the bullish sentiment on freight continued.  2nd half May however looks little bit different, and we are seeing more traders with shipping length in addition to the usual Owners. We therefore expect next deals to be concluded below last done levels.

Aframaxes trading in the North Sea and Baltic enjoyed a pre-Easter fixing rush. On the back of this activity coupled with some injection stems ex Baltic, rates improved with about 10 worldscale points overall.  After the Easter break, the market turned quiet again. In the short term, rates will at best move sideways. However, we expect activity to pick up again moving into the next fixing window and we could see a firmer market again. The Mediterranean and Black Sea market has moved sideways the past week as several offices have been closed for Easter break holidays. TD19 (Cross-Med) has been hovering around 77.5 to 80 levels. Activity has picked from Charterers’ side at the beginning of this week, but although cargoes are coming into the market optimism from the Owners is short lived as there are still enough prompts ships around to take of the steam. Charterers will still enjoy the luxury of seeing several prompt ships available for cross Med voyages in the week to come and we expect rate levels to remain stable.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Western Market
text: We are starting to see a clearer picture of the volume of exports lost to the delays on the Houston ship channel. Exports were curbed by approximately 200,000 barrels per day for 45 days. Keeping 9 million barrels of LPG in the domestic US market. With this in mind some traders found it surprising to see Mt Belvieu prices rise after a slightly smaller than expected, but still a build of 1 million barrels in US inventories. We expect to see maximum exports from US terminals for the next few weeks as the catch up continues,  with the normal lifting schedule to be resumed at all terminals by the beginning of June. South American demand continues its seasonal increase. Importers are having to pay hefty premiums to draw tons to the region to compete with the CFR market in the East. Regarding the Gasmar tender it is still uncertain if they were able to buy anything for second half June arrival.

Suezmax owners managed to keep some momentum in a firmer market leading into the Easter holidays as Charterers rushed to cover stems before the impending prolonged break, TD20 briefly saw returns close to 18k per day. However, inevitably tonnage again built as the market was paused for a few days, thus the early part of this week has seen rates eroding again. We are round the corner from a predicted impending market recovery at the back end of June and surely this is the last chance for Charterers to wrestle control in a downward direction for a while.

comment_type: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
comment_name: Gas Market Weekly Comment - Eastern Market
text: MEG: Following the rise in crude price, May CP price has surpassed April CP, now being $20 higher at 535$ at the time of writing. May/June CP is still in heavy backwardation but continues to narrow from the previous $46 to $28 within this week.  Freight has continuously soared, whereby eroding the potential CFR profits.  FOB lifters without ship length, are keen to resell their FOB’s rather than bringing the CFR volumes to the Far East themselves.  May FOB’s, especially with lifting in the last decade of May, is reported to have been concluded and mid/high single digit discounts to May CP.    FAR EAST: The rally hasn’t ended, and prices are edging up by a day by day basis. Until this Wednesday 23k propane for 1h June delivery was traded at June FEI plus $30.  Cargoes for 2h May delivery is being bid at May FEI plus $50 and no offers seen.  May FEI/CP has narrowed rapidly from minus $20 to near flattish during this week, partly because the tightness in front month for Far East market and also because positions are being rolled into June.  Until backlog delays are cleared thoroughly from US, we will likely see the Eastern tightness extending into 1h June.  Chinese importers have more or less finished their May buying program and are now looking at their June schedule. Recent deal premium levels has varied from $50’s level to $70s on May CP linkage, subject to cargo delivery time range.  PDH margins have been squeezed by higher Propane costs and weaker Propylene demand, we do however expect demand from this sector will stay stable as most units have substantial downstream linkage, yielding higher value products.  Indonesia’s Pertamina was reported to have awarded their two buy tenders on FOB basis, one middle May for lifting ex AG at May CP plus mid-single digit premium and one late May at CP minus.  FPC has awarded their buy tender for 44k propane delivered to Mailiao during 1-10 June at June MOPJ minus high 40s, with 6 offers received. Some players reckon it’s higher than expectations as compared to a window deal on the same day, while others assessed higher value for cargo delivered early June, plus higher freight costs.

The resurrection turned out to be short lived in the VLCC market. After last week’s fixing frenzy, with rates improving by the fixture, things took a turn for the worse again this week. Oil company relets are being marketed an mass, adding to an already populated position list. MEG/China was logged at W42.5 yesterday – yielding a daily return in the low teens, and barely covering OPEX – and further downward risk is evident short term. The Atlantic market is faring slightly better, as owner are reluctant to commit to longer employment at current levels.

Aframaxes trading in the North Sea and Baltic enjoyed a pre-Easter fixing rush. On the back of this activity coupled with some injection stems ex Baltic, rates improved with about 10 worldscale points overall.  After the Easter break, the market turned quiet again. In the short term, rates will at best move sideways. However, we expect activity to pick up again moving into the next fixing window and we could see a firmer market again. The Mediterranean and Black Sea market has moved sideways the past week as several offices have been closed for Easter break holidays. TD19 (Cross-Med) has been hovering around 77.5 to 80 levels. Activity has picked from Charterers’ side at the beginning of this week, but although cargoes are coming into the market optimism from the Owners is short lived as there are still enough prompts ships around to take of the steam. Charterers will still enjoy the luxury of seeing several prompt ships available for cross Med voyages in the week to come and we expect rate levels to remain stable.

Suezmax owners managed to keep some momentum in a firmer market leading into the Easter holidays as Charterers rushed to cover stems before the impending prolonged break, TD20 briefly saw returns close to 18k per day. However, inevitably tonnage again built as the market was paused for a few days, thus the early part of this week has seen rates eroding again. We are round the corner from a predicted impending market recovery at the back end of June and surely this is the last chance for Charterers to wrestle control in a downward direction for a while.

As Easter Holidays is coming closer, it is safe to say that activity is slowing down. Spot fixing interest has now shifted to May-June cargos in both basins and quite a few fixtures has been concluded already.  East of Suez, availability list has shortened significantly, rates, however, haven’t seen any drastic change so far, but Charterers should make notes.  West of Suez, availability consists mainly of sublet tonnage which means that Atlantic might at any stage become short of shipping, should those players with extra tonnage optimise their portfolios. For now, main shipping interest is related to cargoes out of the Mediterranean and should this continue, things might become more active after Easter. In Newbuilding market, Capital Gas has been reported to have exercised their second option for a vessel with HHI giving them a total of six vessels.  On a separate comment please kindly note that right after Easter we will be sending out a GDPR Form for compliance relating to our reports, and in the meantime we wish everyone a Happy Easter!

Despite overall disappointing returns and poor freight levels, there has been a positive trend this week with index gradually up every day. The c5 route is slowly approaching USD 5 pmt whilst c3 remains around USD 13 pmt level with very few charterers active on this route. There is less tonnage left in the Atlantic, resulting in a relatively big increase in the fronthaul rates.  There is generally more interest in  period tonnage although the overall sentiment is expecting a recovery will take more time.

This week brought most of the LNG players back to the grind after last week’s meetings and networking in Shanghai. Activity seem to have “hit the ground running” with a firmer sentiment - from what could have been the lowest level of year 2019  with regards to the intensity of the LNG shipping activities. While the Chinese players dominated the showcasing of their LNG capabilities in the LNG19 conference, this week everybody joined in (traders, exporters, importers alike) and chartered vessels from all basins. This has resulted in some vessels finding the way out from their idling positions and we see a number of sublet vessels that were available, being withdrawn from our availability lists to do internal trades, further reducing the list of tonnage seeking employment.  Despite the recent activities, headline rates remain stable, but with the likelihood of improvements on the ballast bonus figures going forward. We expect full round trip economics for the shipping costs to maybe come before the headline rates improve.  On the newbuilding front, Maran Gas Maritime and NYK again have hit the headlines with both ordering yet another 174,000m3 LNG vessel respectively, with deliveries from DSME for the former and Hyundai Samho for the latter, to be ready within 2022. NYK’s order is reportedly on the back of a long term charter of up to 20 years including optional extension periods.

After a couple of strong weeks, rates are down in both hemispheres. A recovery is, however, anticipated next week as a larger quantity of cargoes has been entering the market in the last couple of days. A transatlantic round voyage currently pays owners about low USD 9,000 per day, while a short fronthaul from the Continent yields about USD 16,000. In the East, a Pacific round voyage pays around the high USD 6,000's. The BPI 4TC-index is down 53 points to 1,074.

The Baltic Index showed negative figures and dropped even further since last week. It was flat and unexcited market across all basins. USG had limited fresh enquiry and trip to Mediterranean/Continent were fixing around USD 12,000. Trip to India was fixed below USD 17,000. Black Sea was not excited, and oversupply of tonnage put more pressure on rates. Continent saw some better supply of fertilizer, and due to mild weather we saw more cargoes coming from Baltic. India and Middle East market was slow due to local holidays. SE Asia showed more coal supply, and there is a hope of quick recovery.

Suezmax owners have had a much more encouraging week, a steady flow of cargoes have enabled a thinning of position lists, West Africa has managed to gain some ground with Td20 upto ws65 with earnings back up above 20k per day, double that of just over a week ago. In the coming weeks some owners will be looking to make their move in positioning tonnage to the East for scheduled drydocking, these ships will likely be a target for Charterers. There is market talk of impending recovery at the end of the 2nd quarter, and the coming weeks may be the last chance Charterers are able to steer the market on favourable terms.

The final stems for the April program in play and it looks like we will end like at same volumes as we have had the last couple of months. Easter holidays in the West next week and many may want to cover prior to it, but volumes remain steady with May stem confirmations a week down the line. There have been moments when market has appeared to firm a little, but it has simply been insufficient activity for all major VLCC routes for it to happen. Earning still about USD 10k/day with owners carefully selecting their preferred voyages to position themselves for the expected upturn later this summer. In the meantime rates appear flat, though with little downside risk from present levels.

Aframaxes trading in the North Sea and Baltic basin have seen a further softening this week, with the surrounding markets more or less in the same state unfortunately not giving owners much leeway in the search of more prosperous business. We see the market bottomed out in the area, but with the last couple of days being a bit busier in the North we expect owners to put pressure on charterers, asking for rates above last done. In the Mediterranean and Black Sea, rates have moved sideways as a rather quiet week has passed. Quiet but steady, as TD19 is reported at levels just above ws80 throughout the week. Tonnage supply is still in charterers favour, however we believe we have seen bottom levels on rates as TCE is getting close to OPEX-levels. We no longer see much of a rate differential between fixtures ex Black Sea and East Med, since transit in Straits has been running smoothly. In the week to come we expect owners to target the right cargoes in order to minimise waiting time and triangulate their vessel in a sufficient manner.
